articles.title: Josh Allen Discusses Message to James Cook After Overtime Fumble in Bills' Thrilling Win vs. Rams
articles.summary: Despite the Buffalo Bills' dramatic 37-34 overtime victory over the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football, many are wondering whether they should be worried about star running back James Cook.
articles.body:
Despite the Buffalo Bills' dramatic 37-34 overtime victory over the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football, many are wondering whether they should be worried about star running back James Cook.

The Bills almost came up short against the Rams after Cook lost a fumble in the red zone in overtime, his second fumble of the game, costing them a scoring opportunity. Luckily for Buffalo, Los Angeles missed a potential game-winning field goal on the ensuing possession, giving the team a last chance at redemption.

After the win, Bills star quarterback Josh Allen was asked about his message to Cook (1:50 mark), and he made it clear that he has the utmost confidence in the ball-carrier, saying, "We don't gotta say nothing to him."

Cook has now fumbled the ball four times this season, losing two of them. His ball security became a glaring issue during the 2025 campaign, in which he fumbled six times in the regular season and once more in the playoffs. His 11 combined fumbles over the last two years are five more than any other running back in the NFL.

At 4-1, the Bills are expected to contend for a spot in the Super Bowl this season, but they will need Cook to avoid turnovers if they hope to finally break through.

Cook will try to have a better showing when Buffalo returns to action against the Las Vegas Raiders (3-2) in a Week 6 road matchup.

articles.title: NFL Panic Meter: Seahawks already showing more cracks than they did last season
articles.summary: The Seahawks' encore from their Super Bowl season is not off to a hot start.
articles.body:
Last season, the Seattle Seahawks lost their Week 1 game. They went 17-2 the rest of the way.

This season, they've lost as many games by mid-October as they did in the final five months of last season.

It's not the end of the world to be 3-2, but there are more issues than you'd like to see. There are definitely more than we saw last season when Seattle steamrolled to a Super Bowl win.

The Seahawks' running game without Kenneth Walker III is an issue. Seattle was a run-first team that played impeccable defense on its way to a Super Bowl last season. That's hard to pull off when you're 30th in EPA ( expected points added ) per rushing play. The decision to move on from Walker when he was a free agent looks awful. Walker is a star for the Chiefs early this season and the Seahawks are getting nothing from their ground game. Maybe Zach Charbonnet can help turn things around when he returns, but he is coming off a torn ACL and was never a star in the offense.

That puts more pressure on the passing game and there are issues there too. Riding Jaxon Smith-Njigba worked great last season, but it's a big challenge to have an effective passing game with just one viable option. Smith-Njigba has 50 targets and no other Seahawk has more than 20. Smith-Njigba has 583 yards while nobody else is over 129. Smith-Njigba's 37 catches are more than Seattle's second, third and fourth top receivers combined. The rest of the wide receivers have 24 receptions total. JSN is a great player and that formula worked great last season, but it's hard to maintain.

When there's no running game and a narrow passing tree, it can put more on the plate of a turnover-prone quarterback. Sam Darnold has come a long way and has shed the bust label forever now that he helped guide a Super Bowl champion, but he still will turn it over too much. Darnold has five interceptions already despite missing almost two full games due to injury. The defense is still elite, but it's not great to be put in bad situations by the offense.

Seattle is still one of the NFL's elite teams. Losing to the 5-0 49ers isn't a terrible result, even at home. But it already looks tougher for them than it did for the entirety of last season.

Panic meter: Some alarms going off, but we'll trust coach Mike Macdonald to figure things out.

Can the Rams overcome awful special teams?

Bad special teams might have cost the Rams a Super Bowl last season. The special teams made huge mistakes in the final two losses to the Seahawks, including the NFC championship game.

The Rams had a field goal blocked in overtime on Monday, allowing the Bills to steal a win. They also missed a field goal in regulation. Rams coach Sean McVay was obviously bothered with his special teams after the game.

"Offensively and defensively we battled. Thought some of the coverage units, we did some really good stuff," McVay said. "Then in the kicking game, especially with our PAT/field goal, not close to good enough. It cost us the game."

But it's not new. The Rams were bad on special teams last season and did little to fix it. Their special teams are 32nd in DVOA . Even if the Rams make a change at kicker it doesn't change everything. This is going to be a problem McVay has to work around all season because he and the front office didn't bother to address it sufficiently in the offseason.

Panic meter: It's hard to be an elite team when you can't trust special teams to not blow games, and that's a big issue for the Rams going forward.

How will Commanders react to horrible tie?

It's fair to wonder how Sunday's end-of-game meltdown will affect the Commanders going forward. Coach Dan Quinn was asked if he worried the management mess in the final minute would cause players to lose confidence in him or the staff, and it's a fair question. Quinn said he didn't think it would.

"I know how tough our team is, the resilience, the toughness," Quinn said, via John Keim of ESPN. "They're able to handle adversity. We've got to get our execution nailed down. We have to be the team that we're capable of being. And that was the message that was loud and clear today."

The Commanders aren't out of anything at 1-3-1 in a bad NFC East. But it will be interesting to track if Sunday's debacle carries over.

Panic meter: The finish of Sunday's game was so horrifically awful, it wouldn't be a surprise if we look back on it as the moment the Commanders' season unraveled.

Jerry Jones said it was too early to consider removing Parker as the Dallas Cowboys' defensive coordinator. Then he hired a coach with 10 years of experience as either a defensive coordinator or head coach in the NFL.

The Cowboys announced that Mike Pettine was added to the staff as a senior defensive assistant. Had that move happened in the offseason, it would have looked like a smart move to support a 34-year-old coach who was a defensive coordinator for the first time. The move happening now, with the Cowboys struggling badly on defense, could be seen as a threat. It's also curious that Parker is heading up to the press box for play-calling, according to Cowboys owner Jerry Jones. They're searching for answers to a bad defense, and none of it can make Parker feel safe.

But Parker and Pettine have a history. Parker was an assistant for the Packers for two seasons while Pettine was defensive coordinator there. Parker tried to talk Pettine out of retirement when he was hired by the Cowboys, but Pettine said no, though there was a standing invitation for him to visit the Cowboys at their practice facility, according to an ESPN report in February . Still, having a longtime defensive coordinator on staff when the Cowboys are 31st in yards allowed and the owner is already being asked if he's considering replacing the current coordinator is a combustible mix.

Panic meter: Pettine isn't coming for Parker's job, but the speculation will be relentless until Dallas' defense turns it around.

How can Justin Herbert survive the season?

The Chargers' offensive line situation is as bad as it gets. The five starters on Sunday were four rookies, none of whom was a first-round pick, and veteran guard Cole Strange, who ranks near the bottom of Pro Football Focus' grades this season.

It's a horrible flashback to last season, when Herbert was the most pressured quarterback in the NFL behind a makeshift line. He was sacked five times Sunday. There's plenty more to come. Herbert has not played well this season, but with Rashawn Slater on injured reserve and Joe Alt dealing with a neck injury, it's going to get worse.

Panic meter: The Chargers can't protect their most valuable asset, which is a major problem. Again.

The Atlanta Falcons are a different team with Penix in the lineup. We saw that in his three games back since he returned from ACL surgery. But then late in Sunday's game there was another injury.

Penix suffered a rib injury on a hard hit, and it was bad enough that Tua Tagovailoa had to take over in overtime. Tagovailoa threw an interception on his second pass of overtime, which showed again how bad the Falcons are without Penix. Penix's injury history is long, dating back to college and including three ACL tears.

Penix could return as soon as Week 6. But there is a growing question if the Falcons can rely on Penix to stay in the lineup, not just for the rest of this season but for when they consider whether to extend his contract.

Panic meter: It had to be disheartening for the Falcons to see Penix dealing with another injury, knowing that part of his story isn't going away.

articles.title: Nick Sirianni's kickoff decision against the Jaguars wasn't as dumb as it looked. Here's why
articles.summary: Sirianni has taken heat following the Eagles' last-second loss to Jacksonville, but a closer look at the rules paint a picture that defends his late-game dec...
articles.body:
Sometimes the conventional wisdom isn't so wise after all.

Let's start with what we know for certain: the Philadelphia Eagles lost their London game against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday when Jacksonville kicked a zero-time-remaining field goal . The Jaguars had that opportunity because with eight seconds remaining in the game and leading by 1, Philadelphia head coach Nick Sirianni, in defiance of prevailing conventional wisdom, opted to kick the ball off to Jacksonville's Ameer Abdullah rather than booting it out of bounds.

Abdullah caught the kick and returned it 53 yards to the Philadelphia 39. From there, Cam Little booted what, for him, is virtually a chip shot to win the game for Jacksonville, 19-17.

Cue the howls of outrage, from the broadcast booth to the internet ( including right here at Yahoo Sports). How could Sirianni make such a boneheaded mistake? He cost his team a win! Fire him before he can get on the plane!

Sirianni only stoked the flames by leaping onto his sword, to combine a couple potent metaphors. "I didn't make the right decision. I lost us that game," he said after the game. "No other way around it. Nothing else to say about it. I didn't do my job good enough in that situation."

Yes, well. Now that emotions have cooled, it's worth taking another look at the situation. And it turns out that indeed there was another way around it, and Sirianni might not have been the one who truly didn't do his job good enough.

The thing with conventional wisdom is, if it relies too much on past evidence rather than current facts, it's less than useless, it's an active hindrance to winning the damn football game. Two key factors have changed significantly in the days since most ex-jock announcers were in the booth: the kickoff ball placement rules, and the strength and accuracy of field goal kickers. Combined, they change the entire calculus for these end-game, up-by-3-or-less scenarios.

There was a time when "kick the ball out of bounds" was perfectly good advice. On a touchback, the ball was placed at the 25, and the offense would have to traverse virtually half the field to get in range for a game-tying or -winning field goal. No more: as of 2024, a touchback was placed at the 30-yard line, and as of 2025 , it's now placed at the 35.

Even more punitive: the dynamic kicking rules, which mandate that a kickoff must land in the designated "landing zone" that extends from the goal line to the receiving team's 20. Miss that, either short or out of bounds, and the ball ends up starting on the receiving team's 40 -yard line.

In short: trying to kick the ball out of the receiving team's reach means it will be spotted, at a minimum, on the 35-yard line … which very quickly brings the next factor into play.

It's no secret that NFL kickers have grown substantially larger and stronger in recent years. Of the eight longest kicks in NFL history — 64 yards or more — five occurred in 2025 or 2026. All except Matt Prater's massive record-breaking 64-yard boot for Denver at home in 2013 happened in the 2020s. (To extend the chip-shot metaphor from above: this is very similar to what's happening in golf today, where players' ability to blast massive drives off the tee is obliterating the need for second-shot strategy. Drive, wedge into the green, move on.)

Now, think about the pure math of the NFL's current field goal situation. A ball set at midfield, directly atop the logo, would be a 67-yard field goal kick. Consider, also, that Little, Jacksonville's kicker, currently holds the record for longest field goal ever kicked at 68 yards, or from his own side of the field.

That means a team with a good field goal kicker now needs only to get from its own 35 to midfield to be in long-but-possible field goal range. And any team that can't pull off a quick out route for 15 yards in less than eight seconds probably doesn't deserve to win anyway.

Regardless of what you think of how these kickoff changes benefit the team with the lead, all of these modifications were made to help juice competitiveness and excitement, which, well … mission damn sure accomplished.

For a concrete comparison of how this could have played out for Philadelphia, we need to go all the way back to Sept. 27, 2026. (We were so young then!) Back then — see if this sounds familiar — Dallas kicked a game-tying field goal against Baltimore with 10 seconds on the clock. On the ensuing kickoff, the Cowboys' Brandon Aubrey booted the ball into the end zone for a touchback.

Baltimore took over on its own 35 with seven seconds remaining, and in case you can't remember that far back, Lamar Jackson quickly hit Zay Flowers for a 27-yard completion immediately followed by a Tyler Loop game-winning field goal . (One distinction: Baltimore had a timeout in its pocket, allowing it to work the middle of the field, whereas Jacksonville did not.)

Some more math: So far in the 2026 season, NFL teams have returned 659 total kicks for an average of 26 yards, per Pro Football Reference . Just 32 returns — about 4.8 percent of all kickoffs — have gone for more than 40 yards. The Jaguars, specifically, have averaged 27.2 yards per return (which includes Sunday). If we assume an average kickoff lands at the midpoint of the landing zone — i.e. the 10-yard line — then the average Jaguars return would start on the 37-yard line. However, that return would eat up significant clock that a simple touchback wouldn't. As valuable as yardage is that late in the game, time is even more so.

So to bring this all back around to the Philadelphia game, and to prepare for the next time this happens: What Sirianni was facing was whether to 1) kick the ball out of the end zone and hand the ball to Jacksonville at the 35-yard line with eight seconds left, leaving the Jags only one midrange completion to get its mutant kicker into range, or 2) kick to a Jacksonville returner, knowing that the odds dictate that the coverage team would bring him down roughly around the same 35-yard line, with only enough time remaining on the clock for a Hail Mary.

The question then becomes which unit do you trust more, your coverage team or your defense? Sirianni made his choice. It didn't pay off, but it wasn't quite as dumb a choice as it may have seemed in the moment. (And, because of the Commanders' later misfire against the Giants, it wasn't the dumbest coaching decision of the day , not by a mile.)

Commentators, media, fans, let's all learn a little something from the Philly Phailure. In football, as in life, the kneejerk, that's-the-way-we-did-it-when-I-played hot take isn't necessarily the smartest one today, not anymore.

articles.title: Jameson Williams' NFL Fine Rescinded After 'Marijuana' Celebration in Lions vs. Bills
articles.summary: Detroit Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams kept his bank account safe for now.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams kept his bank account safe for now.

Per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Williams won both his appeals of $14,926 and $11,941 fines for celebrations in Detroit's Week 2 loss against the Buffalo Bills. For one of the fines, Williams denied his "brief gesture" was offensive and argued that "marijuana is legal in some states if that was the gesture he was making."

"Although I rescinded this fine, please make every effort to celebrate with your teammates in the best professional manner possible," appeals officer Derrick Brooks stated.

Williams was fined for taunting and for an illegal celebration/vulgar act. His $26,867 Week 2 total came before he was fined $23,417 for unnecessary roughness stemming from impermissible use of the helmet during Detroit's 31-24 Week 3 victory over the New York Jets, which brought his season total to $50,284.

Williams had a slow start to the season but appears to have found his groove. He produced six catches for a season-high 102 yards in a Week 4 loss to the Carolina Panthers, and he scored his first two touchdowns of the season in Sunday's 45-21 win over the Arizona Cardinals.

If Williams can continue producing at a steady level, he will add a much-needed dimension to Detroit's offense. The Lions are already tied for the league lead with 32.8 points per game, and Williams appears poised to continue his upward trajectory over the next few weeks.

Now that he's kept his wallet full, Williams can enjoy Detroit's bye in Week 6 before the Lions return to action on Oct. 25 against the Green Bay Packers.

articles.title: Micah Parsons blames Jayden Daniels for clock mismanagement, says Commanders QB 'probably cost' Dan Quinn his job
articles.summary: Parsons didn't hold back on his Bleacher Report show, "The Edge with Micah Parsons."
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers sack artist Micah Parsons won't play Sunday night against his old team , the Dallas Cowboys, but he's nearing his return from the torn ACL that prematurely ended his first season with the Packers.

Despite his on-field absence, his voice is still being heard, including on his Bleacher Report show, "The Edge with Micah Parsons," where the five-time Pro Bowler blamed Jayden Daniels for the Washington Commanders' embarrassing clock mismanagement in the final moments of their 27-27 tie against the New York Giants over the weekend.

"Jayden Daniels probably cost my man Dan Quinn his job, to be honest with you," Parsons said on an episode that was clipped early Tuesday .

Quinn was Parsons' defensive coordinator for three seasons from 2021-23 in Dallas. During that span, Parsons became NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year and earned three All-Pro honors.

Parsons continued: "I'm a big Jayden Daniels fan, but, the reality is, he probably cost a lot of people their jobs this past weekend."

The Commanders (1-3-1) were gifted a chance at a Week 5 win in overtime once the Giants (3-1-1) turned the ball over. Washington recorded the takeaway on New York's second series of the extra frame. On the Giants' first, kicker Dominic Zvada missed a potential go-ahead 46-yard field goal.

Then New York running back Cam Skattebo fumbled an opportunity for Zvada to try one more kick, which could have been a game-winner. Washington, which led 27-13 early in the fourth quarter, quickly reached field-goal range. Instead of spiking the ball to set up a game-winning field-goal attempt, the Commanders opted for one final play before that possible kick.

Daniels dubiously took a sack and stayed on the ground for a few seconds before seemingly remembering the gravity of the situation. Washington had no timeouts, and the clock was ticking. Most of the starting offense didn't appear to have a sense of urgency.

Ultimately, Daniels and Co. scurried to spike the ball, but they couldn't get lined up in time to do so, and the game unceremoniously concluded with the score tied.

"All respectfully, we get coached so much on these situations that I'm a defensive player and this is programmed to me," Parsons said. "I know what to do in those situations." Parsons went on: "There's no way I'm taking a sack with 14 seconds left and no timeouts. And, mind you, it'd be different if Jayden Daniels was a rookie. This is your third year. You've been to the NFC championship game, you've been in big moments before. To me, even after the sack, you're casually getting up. ... I'm like, 'You just took a sack ...' He's not even urgently getting up. "… If people want to say QBs win or lose games, and, as you can see, they just won or lost the game on the QB's hands, this is your job, bro. ... This is your job to be prepared, to understand the game and understand situations. That's in your job profile. And you're telling me, 'Oh, we're going to pay this guy eventually $60 million?' This cannot happen."

"All respectfully, we get coached so much on these situations that I'm a defensive player and this is programmed to me," Parsons said. "I know what to do in those situations."

Parsons went on: "There's no way I'm taking a sack with 14 seconds left and no timeouts. And, mind you, it'd be different if Jayden Daniels was a rookie. This is your third year. You've been to the NFC championship game, you've been in big moments before. To me, even after the sack, you're casually getting up. ... I'm like, 'You just took a sack ...' He's not even urgently getting up.

"… If people want to say QBs win or lose games, and, as you can see, they just won or lost the game on the QB's hands, this is your job, bro. ... This is your job to be prepared, to understand the game and understand situations. That's in your job profile. And you're telling me, 'Oh, we're going to pay this guy eventually $60 million?' This cannot happen."

Daniels was playing in his third game of the season and his first since dislocating his left elbow again . That injury took place in Week 2 at Dallas.

The 2024 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year dazzled at times during his return, particularly with his legs. Wearing a brace on the elbow of his non-throwing arm, he ran for 103 yards and a pair of scores. Plus, the former No. 2 overall pick completed 17 of 25 passes for 199 yards.

His talent remains tantalizing. But more than a season has passed since he piloted Washington to its first NFC title game in 33 years. His durability has been questioned, and, on Sunday, his leadership was put under a magnifying glass .

Quinn took responsibility and admitted that the right call would have been to simply stop the clock with a spike or a throwaway out of bounds . They didn't need to gain more yards; they could have attempted a potential game-winning field goal earlier, Quinn said.

He also told reporters that the end-of-game sequencing "does not fall on" Daniels, who didn't get into specifics about what went down in that fateful situation. In the locker room, Commanders left guard Chris Paul said via 7News DC's Scott Abraham that Washington not having any timeouts left was discussed in the huddle before the final snap, but other players gave less convincing answers when asked about the matter .

"We've got to stop the clock," Daniels said postgame. "We've got to know the situation. We've got to relay that as an offense. It starts with everybody, top down. Ultimately, it's on me."

Some fans wanted more from Daniels at the mic, and so did Parsons.

"I would like to see more accountability myself," he said. "And I'm a player. I'm a big JD5 fan, but that's inexcusable, bro. The lack of urgency, that's something ... I would've had to say something in the locker room. I would've had to come talk to him, like, 'Yo, that's not OK.'"

Parsons emphasized that situations like the one Daniels ostensibly spaced on are drilled home repeatedly during an NFL season.

"Every day," he said. "Like on Wednesday, we bring up end of half four-minute drill. We talk about it. Thursdays, we literally do two-minute situations. We change the clock, change the time, change the point differential. They need a score, gotta-have-it situation, whatever — we do those situations every week. "On Fridays, red-zone situations, we talk about it. What's the mindset? ... We go through all these situations every week, so there's no way that you don't know these situations. We even go through mock games where we walk through these situations. So, to me, this is a lack of preparation, a lack of mentality and a lack of urgency by the man on campus. That just can't happen."

That just can't happen."

While Quinn was at the helm for the Commanders' storybook run to the NFC championship just two seasons ago, he's now 18-20-1 during his stay in Washington. Since a 3-2 start last season, Quinn's Commanders are 3-13-1.

articles.title: Recently unsealed report on coach Brian Flores contains 'racial stereotypes,' according to lawyers
articles.summary: A recently unsealed recruiting firm's report on Brian Flores has multiple examples of “racial stereotypes” and amounts to unlawful retaliation for the coach'...
articles.body:
A recently unsealed recruiting firm's report on Brian Flores has multiple examples of "racial stereotypes" and amounts to unlawful retaliation for the coach's discrimination lawsuit against the NFL, according to his lawyers.

The Korn Ferry report that was made public Tuesday — a copy of which was obtained by The Associated Press — contains a list of six strengths and seven weaknesses which Flores' attorneys say show the league still uses racial stereotypes in hiring and is unlawfully retaliating against the coach for his lawsuit against the league alleging racial discrimination.

The report, which was first published by Front Office Sports , was prepared in connection with the Las Vegas Raiders' coaching vacancy in 2024. Flores is now the defensive coordinator for the Minnesota Vikings.

"The recently unsealed documents demonstrate two unfortunate, but unsurprising, realities," attorney Michael J. Willemin wrote in a statement. "First, that Mr. Flores' decision to hold the league and its teams accountable for systemic race discrimination has been met with unlawful retaliation. Second, discrimination continues to play a significant role in the hiring process for NFL Head Coaches, as evidenced by the fact that the candidate profile prepared for the Raiders leans heavily on racial stereotypes. We and Mr. Flores are committed to eradicating the institutional racism and retaliation that permeates the league, its teams and their partners."

The NFL didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

One of the strengths listed says Flores is a "polished and a good presenter despite growing up in Brownsville, Brooklyn (same as Mike Tyson). He was able to build a strong friendship with a billionaire's son which gave him opportunities to socialize and learn how to build relationships with white-collar and upper-class individuals."

Brownsville is a predominately Black and Hispanic neighborhood in Brooklyn.

One of the negatives says Flores "can fool you with his polish upwards. Has little people skills, lacks self-awareness and can sometimes exhibit erratic behavior. (Former Dolphins quarterback Tua Tagovailoa's) statements have opened the narrative that Brian was "pessimistic and adversarial" and his style "shattered his confidence."

Other negatives listed included that Flores' "personality is unpredictable" and that he "once threatened violence to his GM and made irrational demands during an ownership meeting."

The report goes on to say that a long-term senior executive said Flores "may have changed since, but he was the worst hiring decision we've ever made."

The final negative was that the ongoing litigation related to the coach's discrimination case against the NFL could cause a distraction.

Flores, who is Black, sued the league and three teams in February 2022, alleging the league was "rife with racism" regarding its hiring practices when it comes to Black coaches. Flores had recently been fired from his head coaching job with the Miami Dolphins.

He was later joined in the lawsuit by fellow Black coaches Steve Wilks and Ray Horton.

articles.title: "It was terrible": Donna Kelce shared the exhausting reality of raising Travis and Jason Kelce under one roof
articles.summary: In 2023, Donna Kelce offered a glimpse into the appetite that helped fuel Travis and Jason Kelce’s journeys to NFL stardom.
articles.body: In 2023, Donna Kelce offered a glimpse into the appetite that helped fuel Travis and Jason Kelce’s journeys to NFL stardom. Raising two future Super Bowl champions meant preparing for more than the usual family dinner. The brothers could polish off astonishing amounts of food, leaving their mother to keep the refrigerator stocked and find ways to meet their growing nutritional needs. From whole chickens and steaks to pancakes and peanut butter sandwiches, Donna’s memories reveal how food became an important part of raising two ambitious athletes. Her account also highlights the demands of their busy schedules and the practical ways she supported their sporting dreams.Donna Kelce reveals Travis and Jason Kelce’s enormous appetitesSpeaking exclusively to PEOPLE on October 10, 2023, Donna recalled how much her sons ate during their high school years. Their appetites were so impressive that a regular family meal often required plenty of preparation."They ate a lot," Donna told PEOPLE exclusively of her sons, who currently play for the Kansas City Chiefs and Philadelphia Eagles. "They could sit down and eat an entire chicken in high school each — not together; each one of them could finish a chicken."Keeping food available was a constant task. Donna made sure the refrigerator had plenty of chicken, steak, hamburgers and other meals the boys enjoyed. Milk was another essential, although it rarely lasted long enough."milk was completely gone," she said, explaining that the family needed to buy more every day. Leftovers were equally short-lived, even when someone labelled them or tried to keep them aside.The brothers’ appetites followed them to college, too. During a visit to the University of Cincinnati, Donna asked them where they wanted to eat. They chose IHOP, which she initially expected to be an inexpensive option.Instead, she found herself looking at a table covered with food."So we're sitting down and there's like 18 plates on the table," remembered Donna. "There's steak, there's pancakes — and they devoured it all... You have to remember that they lose pretty much 14 to 15 lbs. every time they play," she continued. "So it gets kind of crazy and you have to replenish that pretty fast."How Donna Kelce kept her sons fuelled for footballFeeding two athletes was not always about elaborate home-cooked meals. With games, travel and other commitments filling their days, Donna often relied on fast food when time was limited."It was terrible, but you had to get from game to game to game," she explained. "We had to go to the store or go through a drive-through. That's all the time we had."She also kept simple snacks ready, including peanut butter and jelly sandwiches and marshmallow treats. Donna wanted her sons to have something convenient to eat between their demanding activities."There wasn't any kind of energy stuff or whatever to give them an extra boost in the second half of a game, so I did that."Her approach was practical: provide filling meals, keep snacks close and make sure her sons had food when they needed it.Years later, Donna’s own travel habits still reflect those lessons. Her partnership with KIND introduced a limited-edition product called Donna’s Purse Snacks, Dark Chocolate Vanilla Cashew Dipped Clusters. The product sold out within 24 hours, according to the report.Donna also explained that she continues to carry snacks while travelling, especially when busy schedules make regular meals difficult. articles.title: Recruiting firm's Brian Flores report 'leans heavily on racial stereotypes,' attorneys say
articles.summary: Attorneys representing Brian Flores say an unsealed report by recruiting firm Korn Ferry contained racial stereotypes about Black NFL coaches.
articles.body:
A report about Brian Flores prepared by recruiter Korn Ferry for the Las Vegas Raiders as part of one of the team's recent coach-hiring cycles was unsealed on Tuesday, Oct. 13.

Attorneys representing Flores say the report "leans heavily on racial stereotypes" that NFL teams use in evaluating Black coaches.

"The recently unsealed documents demonstrate two unfortunate, but unsurprising, realities," Flores' attorney Douglas H. Wigdor told Front Office Sports . "First, that Mr. Flores' decision to hold the league and its teams accountable for systemic race discrimination has been met with unlawful retaliation. Second, discrimination continues to play a significant role in the hiring process for NFL Head Coaches, as evidenced by the fact that the candidate profile prepared for the Raiders leans heavily on racial stereotypes."

Korn Ferry's report was divided into columns that included "strength" and "weaknesses." Flores' attorneys alleged both lists contained racial stereotypes.

That included, on the positive side, a point that implied someone from Brownsville – which is 81% Black and Hispanic – could only succeed by meeting a wealthy individual's family member, as Wigdor explained.

"Polished and a good presenter despite growing up in Brownsville, Brooklyn (same as Mike Tyson)," the Korn Ferry report reads. "He was able to build a strong friendship with a billionaire's son which gave him opportunities to socialize and learn how to build relationships with white-collar and upper-class individuals."

Meanwhile, on the negative side, the Korn Ferry report included a line that Flores "can fool you with his polish upwards." Another of his attorneys, Michael Willemin, described the comment to Front Office Sports as "racially offensive way in which someone might comment upon a Black man being articulate, as though it is surprising for a Black man to be articulate (or, in this case, polished)."

Additionally, Willemin described the following statement as conjuring images of the "angry Black man" stereotype.

"Chip on his shoulder – can be a dictator with players, coaches, and can even be difficult with ownership," the Korn Ferry report read. "His personality is unpredictable – not sure who is going to show up. Failed in how he hires coordinators and staff because he doesn't give second chances or see efforts to improve."

"Needs someone strong at the top to reign (sic) in some of his worst behavior," it continued. "He once threatened violence to his GM and made irrational demands during an ownership meeting. One long-time senior team executive said, 'He may have changed since, but he was the worst hiring decision we've ever made'. Another President of a club refused to talk about him."

The Korn Ferry report also notes that Flores' ongoing litigation against the NFL could be a "distraction," which Willemin cited as evidence of retaliation.

Flores, who is currently the defensive coordinator of the Minnesota Vikings , originally sued the NFL in 2022 . He alleged racial discrimination by the league and several of its teams in the hiring process for new head coaches.

Flores' suit contains claims that teams conduct "sham interviews" with minority candidates to satisfy the league's "Rooney Rule" – which mandates that every NFL team must interview two non-white candidates for every head coach, general manager and coordinator position – despite alleged preferences to hire a white candidate.

Flores' suit was brought against the NFL but also targets the Miami Dolphins , for whom he coached from 2019 to 2021, and three teams that interviewed him for coaching jobs: the New York Giants, Denver Broncos and Houston Texans.

articles.title: NFL suspends Rams LT Alaric Jackson 2 games for punching Bradley Chubb in the face after 'Monday Night Football'
articles.summary: The incident took place on the field after Buffalo's 37-34 overtime win at Sofi Stadium in Los Angeles.
articles.body:
The NFL has suspended Los Angeles Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson for two games after he punched Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb in the face in the aftermath of "Monday Night Football."

In its announcement Tuesday, the league stated that Jackson was in violation of Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1 regarding "any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship."

The incident took place on the field after Buffalo's 37-34 overtime win at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles on Monday. Jackson was exchanging his jersey with a Bills player when Chubb said something to Jackson and pointed at him from a distance.

Chubb turned around and walked away after his comment. Jackson followed Chubb, and the two exchanged words. Jackson then punched Chubb in the face. Chubb's teammates pulled him away from the scene before the incident could escalate further.

ESPN cameras recorded the incident during its postgame coverage.

It's not clear what Chubb or Jackson said leading up to the punch. Jackson had not addressed the incident as of Tuesday. Chubb said this of the incident to the California Post Monday night.

"It was a close game," Chubb said, per the Post. "And, you know, they always catch the second guy, so I let him swing and my teammates held me back and I just chilled."

Tough time for Rams to be without Jackson

The suspension of Jackson leaves the Rams without a key player during a critical juncture of their season.

A Rams team that entered the season as the favorite to win the Super Bowl fell to 2-3 with the loss and will now play its next two games without its most important offensive lineman.

Backup David Quessenberry will replace Jackson at left tackle while Jackson is out, protecting Matthew Stafford's blindside. Head coach Sean McVay confirmed Quessenberry's promotion Tuesday night.

Jackson will miss upcoming against the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders.

Against the Raiders, the Rams will be up against five-time Pro Bowl pass rusher Maxx Crosby. Against the Cardinals, they'll face former Pro Bowler Josh Sweat, who tallied a career-high 12 sacks last season.

After facing the Raiders, the Rams will play the Chargers, Commanders and Cardinals again before a Week 11 bye. They'll need a strong showing in that five-game stretch to remain afloat in the NFC playoff picture.

articles.title: Tom Brady’s charity controversy deepened over $46.5 million in fundraising and $500,000 in yearly grants
articles.summary: Tom Brady built a legendary NFL career, but his charitable work faced uncomfortable questions in 2017.
articles.body: Tom Brady built a legendary NFL career, but his charitable work faced uncomfortable questions in 2017. A report by The NonProfit Quarterly examined the funding behind the former New England Patriots quarterback’s private foundation and its ties to Best Buddies International. The central concern was not simply how much money changed hands, but who supplied it and where it went. Despite Brady’s estimated $180 million fortune at the time, public tax records showed that he had not contributed to his own foundation for a decade, while another nonprofit provided substantial financial support.Tom Brady’s charity faced scrutiny over $500,000 annual grantsBrady established the Change the World Foundation Trust in 2005 with an initial contribution of nearly $500,000, most of which came from him. However, publicly available tax records reviewed by the publication showed no further personal contributions from Brady during the following decade.The foundation’s funding instead relied heavily on Best Buddies International, an organisation that supports people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Its work includes building friendships, expanding employment opportunities and developing leadership skills.Best Buddies reportedly credited Brady with raising $46.5 million for the organisation since 2001. In 2011, it granted his private foundation $250,000. That amount later increased to $500,000 annually, with the arrangement expected to continue.The payments raised questions about whether they represented charitable grants or compensation for Brady’s fundraising efforts. Anthony Shriver, the organisation’s founder, defended the arrangement by describing the payments as “appropriate honorariums” and pointing to Brady’s wider role in promoting the cause.“When I come to Best Buddies events, it’s all about Best Buddies, which is the way I want to keep it while I develop my interests. Would you support helping me pursue my things while I continue to put a lot of energy into your thing?” Brady reportedly said in 2011.The arrangement attracted criticism from charity watchdogs. Art Taylor of the Better Business Bureau Wise Giving Alliance said the charity should explain the payments more clearly. Charity Watch president Daniel Borochoff also questioned whether Brady deserved full credit for philanthropy supported by other organisations.Tom Brady’s TB12 Foundation raised further questionsThe scrutiny extended beyond Brady’s private foundation to the TB12 Foundation, established in 2015 to help promising young amateur athletes access the TB12 Method of training.Its tax filing disclosed connections between the nonprofit and TB12 LLC, Brady’s for-profit fitness and nutrition business. Brady was listed as the foundation’s board president and an owner of the company. The filing also identified TB12 executive Jeffrey Surette as the foundation’s treasurer and clerk. Surette received approximately $154,000 in compensation in 2015, according to the return.These links prompted concerns about whether charitable resources could indirectly support a business associated with the people running the foundation.The 2017 report did not establish that the arrangements were illegal. Instead, it called for greater transparency and accountability over how charitable money was used.The controversy highlighted a broader issue in celebrity philanthropy: public recognition for charitable work can become complicated when donations, private foundations and commercial interests overlap. articles.title: Josh Allen injury update: Bills quarterback’s throwing concerns spark fresh questions after dramatic 37-34 overtime win over Rams
articles.summary: Josh Allen helped the Buffalo Bills escape a tense battle with the Los Angeles Rams, but his performance left questions that a thrilling win could not
articles.body: Josh Allen helped the Buffalo Bills escape a tense battle with the Los Angeles Rams, but his performance left questions that a thrilling win could not erase. Buffalo prevailed 37-34 in overtime, with Allen producing a remarkable display on the ground. Yet his throwing mechanics, recent interceptions and signs of discomfort have drawn fresh attention. The quarterback admitted he had been working through a mechanical issue, while head coach Joe Brady openly acknowledged the team’s passing struggles. With the Las Vegas Raiders next on the schedule, Allen’s health and accuracy have become important talking points for Buffalo.Josh Allen’s throwing mechanics raise injury concerns after Rams winAllen’s comments after the Rams game offered a glimpse into the challenge behind his uneven passing performance. According to The Buffalo News reporter Lance Lysowski, the quarterback acknowledged that he had been working through a mechanical issue and spent too much time thinking about it during the first half.“Bills QB Josh Allen told reporters that he’s working through a mechanical issue with his throwing,” Lance Lysowski of The Buffalo News reported on X. “Decided to stop thinking about it in the second half and let it rip. Wished he had taken more underneath throws early in the game.”Allen completed four of seven passes for 60 yards in the first half and threw an interception to Rams cornerback Jaylen Watson. His accuracy improved after halftime, although his final numbers remained modest by his usual standards. He finished with 12 completions on 19 attempts for 210 yards, one passing touchdown and one interception.Separately, footage from a Bills practice appeared to show Allen bumping his right hand during a drill. A further observation from injury commentator Thigh Doctor raised the possibility of a thumb concern. However, neither observation confirms that Allen has a hand injury, and the reported mechanical issue should not automatically be treated as evidence of physical damage.Joe Brady questions Josh Allen’s passing as rushing saves BillsWhile Allen struggled to find his rhythm through the air, his running ability proved decisive. He recorded 121 rushing yards on 10 carries and scored a rushing touchdown, helping Buffalo secure a dramatic overtime victory.Bills head coach Joe Brady did not hide his concerns about the passing attack after the game.“‘We weren’t good passing the ball tonight.’ – Joe Brady talking about Josh Allen making difference with his legs. ‘When the ball was in his hands he made some critical plays toward the end,'” Jonathan Acosta of WGRZ reported on X.Allen also acknowledged that Buffalo needed to improve its passing execution.“Don’t think we threw it very well, especially in the first half but our team kept fighting. We found a way to win, it’s the first OT [win] I’ve got, so it feels good being on this side,” Allen said.The quarterback’s recent numbers add another layer to the concern. He has thrown four interceptions across his last three games, alongside two passing touchdowns and four rushing touchdowns. He also appeared to limp during the Rams game after previously attracting attention over his knee following a hit against the Los Angeles Chargers.Buffalo improved to 4-1 and moved into first place in the AFC East. Allen’s ability to create plays with his legs remains a major asset, but the Bills will need more consistent passing as they prepare to face the Raiders in Week 6. articles.title: Rams sign CB Damarion Williams to practice squad, cut LB Jamie Sheriff
articles.summary: The Rams added a secondary piece to their practice squad who's bounced around the league for a few years.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams made a pair of practice squad moves, according to the NFL transaction wire, signing cornerback Damarion Williams and releasing linebacker Jamie Sheriff .

Williams, 28, is a 5-foot-10, 183-pound corner who finished his college career at Houston. The Baltimore Ravens selected him in the fourth round (141st overall) of the 2022 NFL Draft. Williams appeared in 14 games as a rookie, totaling 24 tackles (15 solo), one tackle for loss and two pass breakups. He played in one game in 2023. In 15 career games, he has yet to start and has no interceptions or sacks.

Williams has bounced around since the Ravens drafted him in the fourth round in 2022. Baltimore waived him in August 2024, and he later landed with the Seahawks and Buccaneers, spending time on both practice squads. Tampa Bay waived him Aug. 30 and then from injured reserve Sept. 3, making the Rams his fourth organization.

Sheriff, 26, is a 6-foot-1, 254-pound linebacker who played at Mississippi Gulf Coast and South Alabama. Sheriff has appeared in three NFL games: two in 2024, one with Carolina and one with Seattle, and one with the Seahawks in 2025. He has one career tackle, which came in 2025, and is a one-time Super Bowl champion.

Sheriff went undrafted in 2024 and signed with Seattle, was claimed by Carolina the day after Seattle waived him, and played 17 snaps in the Panthers' Week 1 loss. He returned to the Seahawks' practice squad that September and stayed with Seattle until he was waived Aug. 30, making the Rams his third team.

Both moves are practice squad transactions and do not affect the Rams' 53-man roster.

articles.title: Former 49ers practice squad member signed by Jets
articles.summary: Quinton Bell spent the 2026 offseason with the 49ers after bouncing around the league since 2019.
articles.body:
A recent member of the San Francisco 49ers practice squad is headed elsewhere. The New York Jets signed defensive end Quinton Bell this week to their practice squad after the 49ers released Bell on Aug. 30.

The 6-foot-4 and 258-pound Bell recorded four tackles and one special teams stop in preseason action this summer.

The 49ers were the latest stop in a career that has taken Bell across the league after he signed a one-year deal on July 29, 2026. He has appeared in 33 games with three starts over four seasons with Tampa Bay (2020), Atlanta (2022) and Miami (2024-25). In that time, he has totaled 38 tackles (18 solo), one sack, one pass breakup and one forced fumble.

The Las Vegas Raiders selected Bell in the seventh round (No. 230 overall) of the 2019 NFL Draft. Counting the Raiders, the Jets are his sixth organization.

A Long Beach, Calif., native, Bell was a high school track star at Costa Mesa High School. He switched from receiver to defensive end as a senior at Prairie View A&M and earned second-team all-SWAC honors. He became the first Prairie View player drafted since 1980.

articles.title: NFL has been "monitoring developments" in Tyreek Hill case
articles.summary: On Tuesday, a jury entered a mixed verdict in the civil lawsuit filed against free-agent receiver Tyreek Hill by his former wife, Keeta Vaccaro.
articles.body:
On Tuesday, a jury entered a mixed verdict in the civil lawsuit filed against free-agent receiver Tyreek Hill by his former wife, Keeta Vaccaro. The verdict comes at a time when the NFL is investigating Hill for the allegations Vaccaro has made.

"We have been monitoring developments in the matter which remains under review of the personal conduct policy," an NFL spokesperson told PFT on Tuesday night, after the verdict was returned.

The civil verdict is not binding on the league, as to either the counts on which he lost or the counts on which he won. The NFL's investigation is independent of that process.

The key question is whether Vaccaro will cooperate with the NFL. It has no power to issue subpoenas; if, for example, the verdict leads to a prompt settlement, a confidentiality provision could prevent her from talking to NFL investigators.

Regardless, the verdict becomes evidence that the NFL could utilize, along with the transcript of Vaccaro's sworn testimony. It's unclear when the NFL's investigation will conclude, or whether the civil verdict would prompt the league to place Hill on paid leave as the investigation proceeds.

articles.title: Tyreek Hill found liable on two battery counts in divorce battery case, must pay Lakeeta Vaccaro $500,000
articles.summary: A Miami-Dade County jury found Tyreek Hill liable on two counts of battery against Lakeeta Vaccaro, awarding her $500,000 in compensatory damages.
articles.body: A jury found former NFL player Tyreek Hill liable for two separate incidents of battery against his wife Lakeeta Vaccaro and awarded her $500,000 in compensatory damages at the conclusion of their battery divorce trial on Tuesday. The same Miami-Dade County jury that found Hill liable on the two counts of battery also found him not liable on five other counts of battery against Vaccaro, not liable on one count of assault, not liable on one count of committing intentional emotional distress against Vaccaro, and not liable on one count of continuing domestic violence against Vaccaro. Vaccaro's lawyers had earlier on Tuesday also agreed to the dismissal of another count of battery. articles.title: Terrell Owens Reveals He Calls Jameis Winston Weekly Amid Giants QB1 Role & Talks Cowboys Struggles
articles.summary: Hall of Famer Terrell Owens explained that he's been in contact with New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston after he took over as the team's first-string passer.
articles.body:
Hall of Famer Terrell Owens explained that he's been in contact with New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston after he took over as the team's first-string passer.

"I call him every week," Owens said on his Get TO the Point podcast (10:57 mark). "I tell him, I text him. I said, 'Look, I'm going to be your accountability voice.' Like, bro, play like you're supposed to play... I'm not trying to be prophetic by any means, but I know that there's greatness in him."

Winston has served as New York's starter since Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 2.

The Giants have still been able to find success with Winston, holding an early lead atop the NFC East standings. They own a 3-1-1 record, which includes a 2-0-1 mark in his three starts.

Winston has completed 57.6 percent of his throws for 805 yards and six touchdowns compared to three interceptions this season.

Owens also weighed in on the current state of the Dallas Cowboys, the team that he spent three years of his legendary career playing for.

"Yeah, they are definitely in trouble," Owens said (14:33 mark). "If you can't beat the Buccaneers, who are 0 and 4? Yeah, I mean, this is one embarrassing loss after another embarrassing loss. I already told you man with the players at their receiver position there are playmakers and game changers, Dak can only do so much."

The Cowboys have gone 2-3 through their first five games and are coming off a 24-16 loss to a Tampa Bay Buccaneers squad that entered the matchup with an 0-4 record. Buccaneers quarterback Jalon Daniels, an undrafted rookie, was also making just the second start of his career.

Dallas has continued to struggle defensively this season, ranking No. 31 among all teams by allowing 395.4 total yards per game.

The Cowboys have been inconsistent despite Dak Prescott's efficient start to the year, as he's thrown for 1,381 yards and nine touchdowns while getting picked off three times.

articles.title: Josh Allen's Run Game Hyped as Madden X-Factor 'Lighting Up' By Bills WR After OT Win vs. Rams
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills' passing game wasn't connecting in its typical fashion against the Los Angeles Rams on Monday, so Josh Allen turned to his legs.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills' passing game wasn't connecting in its typical fashion against the Los Angeles Rams on Monday, so Josh Allen turned to his legs.

The star quarterback rushed for 121 yards and a touchdown against the Rams, marking the second-highest rushing yard total of his career. On the Bills' final drive in overtime, he scrambled for 32 yards to set up the game-winning field goal.

Bills receiver Trent Sherfield likened Allen's rushing game in moments like that to a Madden player getting his X-factor.

"Well, to me, it's not a look. How I think about it is, it's the Madden player with the X-factor underneath it, and it lights up," Sherfield said, per The Athletic's Joe Buscaglia . "He's the only person that I can look at, and I just picture that X lighting up when he's taking off. It's like when he becomes unstoppable."

Another Bills player, quarterback Shane Buechele, said Allen gets a certain "look in his eye" when he starts to scramble.

"He gets that look in his eye," Buechele said. "Man … It's different. It comes out in these games when it's close, it's back and forth, and the offense needs a spark … you kind of see that look, and then it's a show from there."

Allen finished the game with 210 passing yards, but his legs were the reason he won his first overtime game after previously going 0-7 in overtime games.

articles.title: Tyreek Hill found liable on 2 of 10 domestic violence counts in civil trial with estranged wife
articles.summary: Tyreek Hill's estranged wife was awarded $500,000 in compensatory damages as the trial came to a close on Tuesday night in Miami.
articles.body:
Content warning: This story contains depictions of alleged domestic violence.

Free-agent NFL wide receiver Tyreek Hill was found liable on two of 10 counts related to domestic violence in a civil trial on Tuesday night, according to The Athletic .

As a result, a jury awarded Hill's estranged wife $500,000 in compensatory damages as the trial came to a close in Miami.

Hill was found liable on two of the incidents that included physical evidence. His wife, Lakeeta Vaccaro Hill, alleged that Hill physically abused her after an argument the two got into over a postnuptial agreement that Hill wanted her to sign. There was a photograph shown at the trial that showed a long scratch between her upper chest and neck, per the report. That alleged incident occurred on Jan. 10, 2024.

The second incident took place on April 7, 2025. Hill was spotted on a nanny cam shouting at Vacarro. The incident ended up spilling over into their daughter's room while she was asleep, and Hill's mother called 911 during the incident and told the dispatcher that he had tried to grab the child and leave the condo before she got between the couple.

"I've been in this cycle with him for so long, being pregnant and realizing, 'what am I going to do? How am I going to get myself out of this,'" Vaccaro testified in the trial . "[The abuse] got worse and worse and worse. And it got to a point where, now I'm a new mom. I have to think of her. I have to think about what I'm putting myself through."

The jury found Hill not liable for the other eight counts that were brought up at the civil trial, which included battery, continuing domestic violence and assault. Among other things , Vaccaro alleged at trial that Hill attempted to punch her in the stomach while she was pregnant with their child, that he grabbed and twisted her breasts and once "ended up throwing or shoving" an unlit cigar butt in her mouth.

Hill denied most of the allegations made against him during the trial. He admitted to telling Vaccaro that he could "get people to hurt her" and once pushing her against a wall with such force that it created a hole in the wall, per The Athletic.

Hill has been working to make a return to the NFL, potentially even reuniting with the Kansas City Chiefs . He spent six seasons with the franchise and helped it win Super Bowl LIV. Hill hasn't played since his split with the Dolphins in February, which came after a gruesome knee injury.

It's unclear if Hill would face discipline from the league now that his civil trial is over. An NFL spokesperson told The Athletic on Tuesday night after the verdict that the league has been "monitoring developments in the matter which remains under review of the personal conduct policy."

The NFL's policy does not require criminal charges for a player to be disciplined. But as Hill is currently a free agent, any discipline the league hands down wouldn't kick in until he signs with a new team.

articles.title: JuJu Smith-Schuster Works Out For Chargers Amid LA's Struggles, WR Released by Giants in Preseason

articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers are seeking some offensive help amid a 0-5 start to the 2026 campaign.

The team hosted veteran wide receiver JuJu Smith-Schuster for a tryout on Tuesday, along with four other receivers. Smith-Schuster was released by the New York Giants ahead of the Season.

On Monday, Smith-Schuster worked out for the Minnesota Vikings, who recently signed Odell Beckham Jr. to their practice squad following his release from the Giants.

The veteran wide receiver joined the Giants during the offseason but was cut during training camp while dealing with a knee injury. The 29-year-old spent the last two seasons with the Kansas City Chiefs and recorded 345 yards and a touchdown on 33 receptions last season.

Smith-Schuster was a Pro Bowler with the Pittsburgh Steelers in 2018, but hasn't reached those same heights since. After spending the first five years of his career in Pittsburgh, Smith-Schuster played a season with the Chiefs in 2022, a year with the New England Patriots in 2023 and returned to Kansas City in 2024.

He's hoping to prove he can still be a reliable receiver, and Los Angeles could be the place to do so.

The Chargers' offense has been dreadful to start the season, posting the eighth-fewest yards per game (292.8) and the third-fewest points per game (16.8) as Justin Herbert struggles to find a consistent target.

Tre' Harris is the team's leading receiver but has just 225 yards. Los Angeles' typical top receiver, Ladd McConkey, has struggled with injuries early on and missed last week's game against the Denver Broncos.

Smith-Schuster likely wouldn't be able to match McConkey's production, but he could at least give Herbert another option as the team tries to get things in motion on offense.

Whether the Chargers will take a chance on him remains to be seen.

articles.title: NFL coaches on the hot seat: Who's in the most trouble after 5 weeks?
articles.summary: These three coaches are a collective 2-12-1. One of them just suffered an all-time blunder and another is enduring the worst start he's ever had in his caree...
articles.body:
Week 5 gave us some interesting and perplexing coaching decisions that didn't break in favor of the top men making or overseeing the calls. In an NFL that routinely has high turnover rate among its head-coaching ranks, we're always asking "who's in trouble?"

Yahoo Sports' Frank Schwab , Jay Busbee , Jori Epstein and Eric Edholm each answered that this week as the league approaches completing one-third of the season:

What coach should be feeling the most heat at this point in the season?

Frank Schwab: Dan Quinn screwed up the finish of Sunday's game in a way that wasn't imaginable. Nick Sirianni blew a finish to what should have been a win too. But I don't want to be a prisoner of the moment.

Yes, Todd Bowles shook off some of the speculation about his job security with a great game plan and execution in a season-saving 24-16 win over the Cowboys . Let's also not forget that the weird decision to bypass a field goal in the fourth quarter, which would have given the Buccaneers a 17-point lead, could have cost Tampa that game. It's also just the Buccaneers' third win in their last 14 games.

They're not out of the woods yet at 1-4, starting either undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels or Baker Mayfield coming off a dislocated thumb at quarterback on Sunday against Pittsburgh. Then come pivotal games against the Panthers and Falcons. With one win, Tampa Bay allowed itself a chance to get back in the division race (gotta love the NFC South) but we're just a couple losses away from the Buccaneers being irrelevant again this season and Bowles being on a very hot seat.

Jay Busbee: I grew up a Falcons fan, so my feelings on Dan Quinn, who led the team all the way to the third quarter of a Super Bowl, are complicated and compromised. That said, the mistakes that happened on Quinn's watch at the end of the Commanders-Giants game leave scars not just on a season, but on an entire résumé.

Yes, Quinn engineered a necessary and welcome turnaround of Washington in the post-Dan Snyder era, overseeing that meteoric rise in 2024. But then the turnaround turned back around, and Washington is at the bottom of an already woeful NFC East. You can have occasional misfires if you generally win more than you lose (see: Los Angeles Rams), and you can hang onto your job a while if you're losing but appearing to try (see: Tampa Bay). But losing in embarrassing fashion? Becoming the butt of the league's jokes? Yeah, that's the kind of public humiliation that gets you booted. It was a good run, Dan, but don't make any DoorDash orders that will take longer than a half-hour to arrive.

Jori Epstein: I tend to view job security in the NFL as the result of several factors. A team's record of course is one. But there's more. How does the performance of a losing team compare to expectations for the team's position in the lifecycle of roster building? Were the losses gritty and borderline-moral victories, or were they embarrassing — for coaches, players and at times even team ownership? What other changes could come before changing a head coach? A head coach who has already tried to salvage a project with coordinator turnover has fewer options left.

With that formula, the Washington Commanders' Dan Quinn and Los Angeles Chargers' Jim Harbaugh seem the most susceptible right now. Each team has a quarterback with experience and talent (yes, Jayden Daniels missed time with a dislocated elbow, but Washington's lone win came in his absence); each coach is in at least his third season. Harbaugh hired offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel to salvage an offense that currently ranks 30th in scoring and 25th in yardage; Quinn hired defensive coordinator Daronte Jones to modernize a defense that currently ranks 30th in points allowed and 23rd in yards.

On the Chargers' front, Harbaugh has gone from spats with reporters earlier in the season to this week saying he "can't think of a time I've ever been more mad at myself" than his decision to go for it on fourth-and-1 from his own 41 in the fourth quarter. The Broncos capitalized on the short field to tie the game and score 13 unanswered points en route to a road victory.

The Commanders infamously botched their overtime game mechanics so thoroughly that they couldn't even attempt the game-winning field goal. Quinn has said he was "furious" and minority team owner Magic Johnson tweeted that he was in "total disbelief."

In an impatient league, seats warm quickly.

Eric Edholm: Like, right now now? I'd say Dan Quinn, fair or not. The sight of an angry, helpless Quinn, tangled in his headset cords Sunday, was striking. He'd just witnessed his supposed franchise QB run the clock down to zero, with a chance to win the game, turning it into a shocking tie. Minority owner Magic Johnson posting that he was "in total disbelief" told you all you needed to know about the temperature around Quinn now. Whatever goodwill he earned with the home win over the Seahawks evaporated in that fateful moment against the Giants.

You could make a case for 0-5 Jim Harbaugh being on a hotter seat, but I think Quinn is the hot-seat name of the week because of how that game went down. At 1-3-1, there's not a ton of wiggle room, even in the much-maligned NFC East, and a blowout loss Monday night at San Francisco could be very concerning for Quinn, with the Commanders set to go on bye.

Josh Harris strikes me as a team owner who won't get too emotional about a coaching change, even if he was part of the group that brought in Quinn. The Commanders have a lot to figure out and fix in short time to keep their coach off the proverbial seat.

articles.title: “It is so very important for me to help support”: How Donna Kelce used Jason and Travis Kelce’s NFL fame to support their hometown schools through a T-shirt fundraise

articles.body: Donna Kelce found a way to turn the attention around Jason and Travis Kelce's NFL rivalry into support for their hometown school community. In Oct. 2023, she teamed up with her sons and apparel brand HOMAGE to launch a T-shirt fundraiser for the Heights Schools Foundation in Cleveland Heights, Ohio. The design carried a message familiar to NFL fans, but the cause behind it was personal to the Kelce family.The shirt read “Mama Kelce: Rooting for the Offense,” a playful nod to Donna's refusal to choose between her sons. A portion of the proceeds supported the foundation, which provides scholarships, teacher grants and programmes for students and staff in the Cleveland Heights-University Heights school district. Donna Kelce used her sons' NFL spotlight to give back to their hometownThe Heights Schools Foundation announced the fundraiser on Oct. 24, 2023, after HOMAGE unveiled the design during the Oct. 22 Eagles-Dolphins game. Jason graduated from Heights High in 2006, while Travis graduated in 2008. Both went on to build successful NFL careers, with Jason playing for the Philadelphia Eagles and Travis for the Kansas City Chiefs.For Donna, the fundraiser was about recognising the people who helped raise her sons. In comments to The Philadelphia Inquirer, published on Nov. 18, 2023, she explained why supporting the foundation meant so much to her.“It is so very important for me to help support Cleveland Heights School Foundation,” Donna said.She credited the teachers, coaches, students and parents who helped her and her husband, Ed Kelce, teach their sons lessons beyond the classroom. Donna specifically highlighted inclusion, embracing differences and equality.She also expressed hope that the foundation would continue helping students pursue opportunities they might not otherwise have.The fundraiser gave fans a way to support that mission while celebrating the Kelce family. The shirt featured a caricature of Donna in a design that captured her position as the mother of two competitive NFL players. Rather than picking a side, she backed both sons and their shared hometown.Donna Kelce refused to choose between Jason and Travis KelceThe shirt also reflected a running question Donna faced whenever her sons played against each other: which team would get her support?In a statement published by the Heights Schools Foundation on Oct. 24, 2023, Donna explained how the design reflected her feelings about Jason and Travis.“In our family there is no favorite child, although Jason and Travis may like to joke otherwise,” she said.Donna added that she was proud of both sons and wanted to use some of the attention surrounding their success to help others. She described the opportunity as a way to give back to the Cleveland Heights community, which had supported her family while the boys were growing up.HOMAGE founder and CEO Ryan Vesler also praised Donna's commitment to the community in the foundation's October 24 announcement. He said the company was honoured when she approached it about creating a shirt to benefit the Kelces' hometown.The fundraiser supported a school district where more than 71% of students received needs-based assistance.
