articles.title: 'Football 301' diagnoses fatal flaws of 6 NFL contenders: What could derail Bills, Chiefs, Seahawks and more?
articles.summary: Not even the best teams in the league are perfect. Yahoo Sports' Nate Tice and The Athletic's Derrik Klassen explore what could go wrong for some Super Bowl...
articles.body:
In this week's episode of Yahoo Sports' "Football 301" podcast, host Nate Tice and guest Derrik Klassen of The Athletic took a microscope to the NFL's contending teams and identified the fatal flaws that could keep each from grasping the Lombardi Trophy.

Here's a thorough breakdown of what could trip up each contender.

Despite a surging pass rush and another dynamic year from QB Josh Allen, the soft underbelly of this Bills roster is the coverage unit. Klassen pointed out that the corners and safeties aren't making the grade, notably with players like C.J. Gardner-Johnson — a red flag signing for a would-be contender. There's hope in the front four, but as Tice drilled home, the AFC playoffs will force you to beat elite QBs three weeks running.

With Buffalo's defense currently 28th in success rate and 30th in EPA, the risk of getting torched is painfully real. Unless the pass rush can dominate, expect shootouts and potential heartbreak in January.

Fatal flaw : Offensive line depth and durability

With talent at the skill positions and creative, adaptable coaching, the Jags look dangerous. But their hopes may rest on a precarious offensive line. Klassen highlighted the myriad dominoes that had to fall into place to make this line work, and the recent injury to their best lineman, left tackle Anton Harrison, puts them on red alert. The run game has survived on scheming and quarterback talent, not domination in the trenches, and stats like being 28th in QB hits allowed and 30th in yards before contact on run plays underscore the imminent danger.

Fatal flaw : Lack of downfield speed and explosiveness in passing game

With Tyquan Thornton out for an extended period with an ankle injury, the Chiefs' passing attack risks becoming horizontal and cramped. That's dangerous for a team built around stretching defenses, as Klassen argued.

While the run game has thrived, and Patrick Mahomes can still make magic, Thornton was KC's only real downfield threat. Even the highly touted Xavier Worthy hasn't shown that same top-end juice. Stats confirm it: with almost no plays breaking 20 mph among receivers outside Thornton, the Chiefs could be reduced to a "dink-and-dunk" unit.

Fatal flaw : Inflexible, predictable offense with a capped run game

Tice and Klassen discussed how the Bengals have reverted to their old spread, shotgun-only offense, with little diversity in look or concept. When forced to run, they rely on RPOs, which trade blocking for flexibility and cap explosive play potential. As defenses catch up and scheme specifically for the Bengals' flavor of spread, the games inevitably become tight, with the deep ball to Ja'Marr Chase the only real bailout. As Tice put it: "It's tough to make 10 good decisions in a row against a great defense."

Fatal flaw : Sam Darnold regression and no offensive "Plan B"

Per Klassen, the Seahawks managed to win last year with Darnold threading the needle — burning defenses on big explosives. This year, Darnold's turnover rate has ballooned, his sack rate is up, and his average depth of target has cratered. The run game has suffered from injuries, and auxiliary pass-catchers outside of Jaxon Smith-Njigba haven't stepped up. Without explosives, Darnold isn't the kind of QB to nickel and dime down the field. The formula worked in 2025, but with the supporting cast banged up and his confidence flagging, this offense could struggle hanging with the best again.

Fatal flaw : Undefined offensive identity and inconsistency

With the defense playing at an elite level, all eyes land on whether the Vikings' offense can find a steady footing. The run game is a work in progress, the o-line is banged up and QB Kyler Murray's style introduces volatility. There are flashes — especially when weapons like Justin Jefferson are healthy — but overall the offense feels "grab bag," per Klassen, and is prone to stalls and third-and-longs, leaving it too dependent on Murray heroics or play extension.

For more NFL insight, tune into " Football 301" on Apple , Spotify or YouTube .

articles.title: Tua Trolled By Ravens' Humphrey, Says Kyle Hamilton 'Knew' He Was Going to Pick Off Falcons QB
articles.summary: When Atlanta Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa came in for Michael Penix Jr. in overtime against the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday, Kyle Hamilton was celebrating.
articles.body:
When Atlanta Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa came in for Michael Penix Jr. in overtime against the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday, Kyle Hamilton was celebrating.

Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey said the safety was excited because he "knew" he was going to get an interception.

"He knew he was gonna get a pick," Humphrey said. "He literally was like, 'Oh, he finna throw it to me.' Like, he was so excited. It was the most excited I've probably ever seen Kyle."

Hamilton was right, as he intercepted Tagovailoa's second pass of the drive to seal the win for Baltimore.

Tagovailoa threw a career-high 15 interceptions with the Miami Dolphins last season, and so far, his Falcons tenure isn't off to a great start. He appeared in his first game for Atlanta on Sunday after Penix went down and threw a costly interception.

Whether Tagovailoa will be back on the field next week remains to be seen, but if he gets the nod, he'll look to make up for the pick on Sunday.

articles.title: Jury Finds Tyreek Hill Liable for 2 Battery Counts, Awards $500,000 to the NFL Star's Estranged Wife
articles.summary: MIAMI (AP) — A Miami jury on Tuesday found Tyreek Hill liable for two counts of battery but not liable for the eight remaining claims made by Lakeeta Vaccaro — ending the high-profile civil trial involving the NFL wide receiver and his estranged wife.
articles.body:
MIAMI (AP) — A Miami jury on Tuesday found Tyreek Hill liable for two counts of battery but not liable for the eight remaining claims made by Lakeeta Vaccaro — ending the high-profile civil trial involving the NFL wide receiver and his estranged wife.

Hill, who has played for the NFL's Kansas City Chiefs and Miami Dolphins, was found liable for two counts of battery — one stemming from an incident in January 2024, and another from April 2025. The jury awarded Vaccaro $500,000 in compensatory damages but did not award her punitive damages.

The jury found Hill not liable for eight other counts that included battery, assault and continuing domestic violence.

Hill, wearing a dark polo shirt, embraced one of his attorneys and shook hands with others following the verdict before leaving the courtroom by himself.

It wasn't immediately clear what the verdict means for Hill's return to the NFL. He is still working his way back from a dislocated knee and torn ligaments suffered in September 2025 while he was with the Dolphins, but his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, has indicated that he could be ready to play by November.

articles.title: Ranking the NFL's 5 True Super Bowl Contenders After Week 5
articles.summary: The first five weeks of the 2026 NFL season have revealed a handful of legitimate Super Bowl contenders. These teams' championship prospects are reflected in the updated FanDuel Sportsbook odds.
articles.body:
The first five weeks of the 2026 NFL season have revealed a handful of legitimate Super Bowl contenders. These teams' championship prospects are reflected in the updated FanDuel Sportsbook odds.

Although just two teams opened the year at 10-1 or shorter odds, five squads now fall into that range heading into Week 6.

Here's a look at where each of these top contenders currently stands and where they began the year on the odds list.

Although long shots can win a Super Bowl, it's rare to see a team that went into the season with 11-1 odds or longer accomplish the job. The reigning champion Seattle Seahawks, who opened 2025 with 60-1 odds to lift the Lombardi Trophy, were one of just four teams since the start of the 2013 campaign to pull off the feat.

Opening as an extremely short favorite hasn't been ideal either. Over the last 30 years, the 20 teams that had 5-1 or better preseason Super Bowl odds came up short all 20 times .

With that in mind, let's rank—based on key factors such as how they've started, how they project to finish, potential to pull off a blockbuster trade before the deadline, playoff experience and injuries—the five "true" Super Bowl contenders that have emerged over the first five weeks of the 2026 NFL season.

First-year head coach Jesse Minter has the Baltimore Ravens in strong position to compete for a Super Bowl, getting off to a scorching 4-1 start and taking control of the AFC North after ripping off a three-game winning streak.

Despite barreling towards a playoff berth, Baltimore's hopes of raising a third championship banner remain tied to the shaky health of Lamar Jackson.

The Ravens secured a clutch Week 5 victory over the surging Atlanta Falcons with their star quarterback sidelined, but there is almost no chance the club can go all the way without having the two-time NFL MVP at or near full strength.

Jackson missed Week 5 with an ankle sprain he picked up in the first half of a Week 4 win over the Tennessee Titans. The NFL Network's Ian Rapoport revealed there is a chance the signal-caller could be back for the team's impending matchup versus the Browns, but managing Jackson's long-term health should be of the utmost importance to Baltimore.

The Ravens have gone just 7-11 without Jackson in the lineup since 2019, including a 2022 Wild Card round loss to the Cincinnati Bengals. The team managed to topple the Falcons with Snoop Huntley as the starter, but it can't be expected to realistically reach the playoffs without Jackson starting a vast majority of games—let alone navigate past the elite opponents it will come up against in the postseason.

Jackson was sidelined four games and was limited in several others due to injuries last year, ultimately dooming the Ravens to their first playoff-less campaign since 2021—a season in which the star QB also missed extensive time.

While the Ravens have most of the pieces in place to go on a title run, it's becoming tougher to trust in Jackson's ability to stay healthy enough to see it through. If Jackson can shake the injury bug and get to the playoffs near 100 percent, Baltimore will be as tough an out as any. If he's hobbled or sitting out, the Ravens won't have the firepower to get past the Divisional round.

The Kansas City Chiefs are trying to make sure last year's disappointing 6-11 campaign gets remembered as an outlier in their dynastic run. They're off to a strong start, making it to their Week 5 bye undefeated and remaining one of just three unblemished teams heading into Week 6.

Kansas City's shrewd free-agent pickup of Kenneth Walker III has been a revelation for a team that has struggled to move the ball on the ground in recent seasons.

The reigning Super Bowl MVP has already tallied 621 yards and six touchdowns from scrimmage, helping balance out an offense that desperately needed to support quarterback Patrick Mahomes during his return from a season-ending ACL tear.

Despite having Walker, Mahomes and several other standouts with championship pedigrees such as Travis Kelce and Chris Jones, the Chiefs still shouldn't be considered the favorites to win a fourth Super Bowl in eight seasons.

Kansas City has yet to be truly tested in 2026. Their victories have largely come against inferior opponents, including the still-winless Miami Dolphins. The Indianapolis Colts and Las Vegas Raiders—two teams unlikely to even make the playoffs—hung tough with the Chiefs, only losing by three points apiece.

The Chiefs' real challenge will come in the back half of the season, especially between Weeks 12-16 when they square off against five consecutive potential playoff opponents in the Buffalo Bills, Los Angeles Rams, Cincinnati Bengals, New England Patriots and San Francisco 49ers.

If they can get through that stretch with a winning record, then it will be time to truly believe in this group's championship chances.

The Los Angeles Rams have disappointed out of the gate in 2026, but there are still plenty of reasons to believe they can turn things around and deliver on their immense Super Bowl hype.

While the Rams dropped back below .500 following a 37-34 defeat to the Buffalo Bills in Week 5, the offense had one of its best performances of the campaign. The team posted a season-high point total, Matthew Stafford played at an MVP level, and a rejuvenated Puka Nacua caught 17 of his 24 targets for 138 yards and a touchdown.

The offense, which currently ranks No. 1 in total and passing yardage, shouldn't be a problem and the defense hasn't been terrible either. Even without reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett in the mix due to a knee injury, L.A. still ranks No. 3 in total defense and No. 2 in passing defense.

The main problem the Rams' defense has been contending with is the short fields opposing offenses have received as a direct result of a problematic special teams game—an issue shaping up to be the Rams' Achilles heel in 2026.

Los Angeles botched a golden opportunity to topple the Bills with an overtime field goal, allowing the pivotal kick to be blocked. It was the final mishap in yet another tough night for the special teams unit, which began the game having its opening kickoff get returned for 70 yards.

The Rams' special teams accumulated minus-110 percentage points of win probability added last year and are already at minus-104 percentage points in 2026.

Head coach Sean McVay appears intent on ironing out these issues. He admitted that "it's been a while since I've been this pissed after a game" following the loss to Buffalo and revealed that he plans to "evaluate everything" around the kicking game.

If L.A. can find a way to sort out this abysmal special teams unit, the team will be in prime position to go on a huge winning streak and set itself up to make a Super Bowl run. If it can't, the Rams will come up short once again.

The Buffalo Bills made some sweeping offseason changes in the wake of yet another disappointing playoff defeat in the Josh Allen era.

Those brash decisions appear to be paying off, as the squad has jumped out to a 4-1 start and looks every bit like the AFC's top Super Bowl contender.

New head coach Joe Brady has the offense firing on all cylinders following his promotion from offensive coordinator. The Bills are putting up over 400 yards per game and are tied for the league lead by scoring an average of 32.8 points per game.

Josh Allen is the front-runner to take home his second NFL MVP award, tallying 1,249 passing yards and seven passing touchdowns in addition to the 239 yards and whopping eight scores he's rung up on the ground. Star running back James Cook has taken his game to another level, gashing opposing fronts for 532 yards and five touchdowns on his 95 totes.

Injuries haven't slowed Buffalo down either. Despite missing key contributors such as defensive stalwart Ed Oliver and prized offseason acquisition D.J. Moore, the Bills still managed to knock off the Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams in Week 5. The statement win came on the heels of their lone loss of the 2026 campaign, a narrow 29-26 defeat to the rival New England Patriots.

While Buffalo doesn't boast the most talented lineup on paper and still has some issues—most notably in the secondary—to iron out before the trade deadline, this team has the makeup of a Super Bowl winner.

Whether they can finally realize that potential after so many heartbreaking playoff losses remains to be seen, but it would be unwise to count the Bills out while Josh Allen and co. are playing at their current level.

The San Francisco 49ers are one of just two teams to open the 2026 NFL season with five victories, an incredible run made even more impressive by the sheer number of injuries the team has withstood since the start of training camp.

Despite being forced to go without a plethora of their key contributors—a growing list that includes Nick Bosa, Ricky Pearsall, Christian Kirk, De'Zhaun Stribling, Kyle Juszczyk and Deebo Samuel—for various stretches, the 49ers have managed to remain unbeaten through it all.

The rise of quarterback Brock Purdy to a legitimate NFL MVP candidate has been a driving force behind this incredible run.

Purdy has looked like the NFL's best passer this season, connecting on 98 of his 142 throws for an efficient 1,196 yards and a league-leading 13 touchdowns. He's limited his turnovers to just two interceptions, been sacked a meager three times and contributed 128 yards and a score on 25 carries.

The defense has largely been doing its job as well. San Francisco ranks No. 3 in scoring defense and boasts a top-10 passing, rushing and total defense. These figure to improve as the team gets Bosa and other contributors on that side of the football back in the coming weeks.

These Niners are clearly motivated after being embarrassed in last year's playoffs, exacting their revenge against the Seattle Seahawks with a hard-fought 32-29 victory over their NFC West rivals. The win gives them a major leg up in the divisional race and has them trending toward earning the No. 1 seed in the conference.

After a number of close calls during Kyle Shanahan's tenure as head coach—including two NFC Championship Game defeats and a pair of Super Bowl losses since the start of the 2019 season—San Francisco is a genuine threat to break through and capture its first Lombardi Trophy in over three decades.

articles.title: Packers’ Micah Parsons drops truth bomb on NFC East’s brutal Week 5

articles.body:
Despite playing without Micah Parsons , the Green Bay Packers have managed to maintain a 3-2 record as their star defensive player continues recovering from surgery to repair a torn ACL . However, while his current team has made a promising start to the season, Parsons has also been keeping an eye on the struggles of his former NFC East rivals.

All four NFC East teams, the New York Giants, Washington Commanders, Dallas Cowboys, and Philadelphia Eagles, failed to secure a win in Week 5. Parsons did not hold back when discussing the overall quality of football being played by his former rivals.

"It's been bad ball," Parsons said in an interview with Bleacher Report.

Beyond the division's overall struggles, Parsons also weighed in on the Commanders' recent matchup against the New York Giants. Washington had an opportunity to secure a victory in overtime but failed to execute on the final play, leaving the game tied at 27-27.

Parsons is now in his second season with the Packers after spending the first part of his NFL career with the Cowboys. His former team has also struggled to find consistency this season, sitting at 2-3 after its first five games.

Meanwhile, Green Bay continues to wait patiently for Parsons to make a full recovery. The star pass rusher has not yet received medical clearance to return to practice as he works his way back from the serious knee injury. His absence has created a significant challenge for the Packers' defense.

However, there is some optimism surrounding his progress. According to longtime NFL insider Ian Rapoport, Parsons could return to practice next week.

The Packers are preparing to face the Dallas Cowboys next. But Parsons will once again be unavailable for the highly anticipated matchup against his former team.

Missing the opportunity to face his former team may be disappointing, yet the Packers are unlikely to take unnecessary risks with their defensive star's recovery.

articles.title: ‘Time for That Ceremony,’ ‘When Does That Guy Get His Red Jacket?’ — Falcons Fans Once Again Mount Calls to Induct Michael Vick Into The Ring of Honor

articles.body:
Michael Vick last played for the Atlanta Falcons in 2006, but he can still get the place started. The former No. 1 overall pick sounded the train horn before Sunday night's 30-23 overtime loss to the Baltimore Ravens, the same night former defensive end John Abraham joined the team's Ring of Honor.

However, for some fans, it was a cue to ask when Vick gets a spot in that same Ring.

Falcons' Post Sparks Calls for Michael Vick's Induction

The message itself left plenty of room for interpretation, with the team writing simply "Falcons Family" on Monday night.

That family grew by one the night before. Former coach Mike Smith introduced Abraham at halftime, and fellow Ring of Honor members Warrick Dunn and Roddy White handed him his jacket.

Abraham, whose 68.5 sacks are officially recognized as the most in team history, became the 15th member of the Ring that already includes Matt Ryan, the franchise's all-time leader in passing yards and touchdowns, and now its president of football.

But as Falcons fans took notice of the team's post, there were renewed calls for Vick to get his rightful place in the annals of the team's history.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

"When does that guy get his red jacket?" one Falcons fan replied, asking when Vick will get his due.

One fan replied to the same post, writing that the fans "need" Vick in the Ring of Honor.

Another account underlined that same thought, writing it's time to "put Vick in the Ring of Honor!!"

Michael Vick Still Waiting Since Arthur Blank's 2017 Ring of Honor Remark

The idea is hardly new. On June 12, 2017, Falcons owner Arthur Blank honored Vick and White as retired former players at a ceremony in his Buckhead offices. Blank said his family foundation was dedicated to giving second and third chances and that he had no problem honoring Vick.

"Both, given their records as Falcons players and their careers, they would certainly be considered for that," Blank said when asked whether the two were Ring of Honor possibilities. More than nine years later, Vick is still waiting, and it appears fans have had enough of it.

Another fan wrote, "Time for that ceremony," urging the franchise to finally do what's right.

Vick is now the head coach at Norfolk State, whose Spartans beat Virginia Lynchburg 62-0 on Saturday to improve to 4-3, the day before his return to Atlanta.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

"Did him dirty, now we are using him to elevate the brand," another fan griped, aiming criticism at the franchise.

Vick, of course, never played for the Falcons again after pleading guilty to a federal dogfighting conspiracy charge in August 2007. He was sentenced to 23 months, serving about 19 months in prison and another two under home confinement before returning to the NFL with the Philadelphia Eagles in 2009.

Not everyone was sold back when Blank made his remarks in June 2017. The Atlanta Journal-Constitution's Steve Hummer wrote the day after the 2017 ceremony that he would not put Vick's name in the rafters. He also wrote that the Ring has no hard and fast standards and that, if not for Vick's fall, the Falcons would not have Ryan.

As things stand, the next spot is already spoken for. The late Bill Fralic, a three-time All-Pro guard, will become the 16th member when the Falcons host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 16.

articles.title: Alaric Jackson: NFL suspends Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman for striking Buffalo Bills' Bradley Chubb after Monday night NFL game
articles.summary: NFL suspends Alaric Jackson after he struck Bradley Chubb following Monday Night Football; Jackson set to miss two games but will appeal; 49ers' Dre Greenlaw also suspended for headbutt
articles.body:
Starting left tackle Jackson struck Chubb after the two exchanged words following the Bills' 37-34 overtime victory over the Rams at SoFi Stadium.

Jackson was doing a jersey swap with another Bills player when Chubb spoke to him then walked away. Jackson followed and confronted Chubb before throwing a strike that knocked Chubb's hat off his head.

In a press release, the league called Jackson's blow "an act of unsportsmanlike conduct."

Jackson is set to miss games against Arizona and Las Vegas but will appeal the league's ruling, Rams coach Sean McVay said.

"Have to make better decisions than that," McVay said. "I spoke with him. We'll keep that in-house. ... I want to understand the totality of the situation. I'm not condoning by any means, but I want to gather all the information."

David Quessenberry will be the Rams' starting left tackle during Jackson's absence, McVay said. The 36-year-old veteran has played just 128 offensive snaps over the previous two seasons, and he hasn't started an NFL game since 2023.

49ers' Greenlaw suspended one game for headbutt

San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw was also suspended for one game after headbutting Seattle's Ernest Jones IV following a late hit on the Seahawks sideline.

Greenlaw will miss San Francisco's game next Monday night against Washington.

We haven't seen much more than rainfall impact the early schedule, but as temperatures drop and fall winds swirl, that will change.
articles.body:
We're nearly halfway through October, which means that Halloween is right around the corner and weather is about to become a factor in many NFL games. We haven't seen much more than rainfall impact the early schedule, but as temperatures drop and fall winds swirl, that will change.

Of course, it's not as if the 2026 season needs an added jolt of unpredictability. We've already seen some strange occurrences—like the Washington Commanders forgetting to kick a field goal before overtime expired—and unexpected results.

The Cleveland Browns and Las Vegas Raiders both have a better record than the Los Angeles Rams.

Here, we'll take an early look at the Week 6 slate, the latest odds, and the most accurate forecast information from The Weather Channel and make a few predictions.

Seattle Seahawks (-2.5) at Denver Broncos

Houston Texans (+2.5) vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (in London)

Chicago Bears (-3.5) at Atlanta Falcons (Retractable Roof)

Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns

Tennessee Titans (+6.5) at Indianapolis Colts (Retractable Roof)

New York Jets (+7.5) at New England Patriots

New Orleans Saints (-1.5) at New York Giants

Carolina Panthers (+1.5) at Philadelphia Eagles

Pittsburgh Steelers (-2.5) at Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Forecast: Partly Cloudy, Winds up to 18MPH, High of 81°F

Arizona Cardinals (+12.5) at Los Angeles Rams (Dome)

Los Angeles Chargers (+8.5) at Kansas City Chiefs

Buffalo Bills (-5.5) at Las Vegas Raiders (Dome)

Dallas Cowboys (+1.5) at Green Bay Packers

Washington Commanders (+7.5) at San Francisco 49ers

Forecast: Partly Cloudy, Winds up to 15 MPH, Low of 52°F

Bye Weeks: Cincinnati Bengals, Detroit Lions, Miami Dolphins, Minnesota Vikings

The Week 6 schedule will kick off with an intriguing matchup between the Denver Broncos and Seattle Seahawks, two teams that were among the NFL's final four last season.

Seattle has looked every bit like the defending Super Bowl champs for most of the season, but mistakes have cost them in games against the Washington Commanders and San Francisco 49ers. The Broncos, meanwhile, haven't looked as formidable as they did last season. The Denver offense has been especially disjointed, though its defense finally had a strong showing in Week 5.

Several other marquee matchups will highlight the week, including an early afternoon battle between the Chicago Bears and the Atlanta Falcons. Both teams lost in Week 5, and the Bears got blown out by the rival Green Bay Packers. Both will be looking to rebound in a big way.

The Chicago Bears may also have star quarterback Caleb Williams (hamstring) back in the lineup after he came close to returning on Sunday.

There's a chance that the Baltimore Ravens will also have their starting quarterback in Week 6 for a surprisingly important game against the Cleveland Browns.

Lamar Jackson missed Week 5 with an ankle injury, but the Ravens were able to mount a comeback against the Falcons with Tyler Huntley at quarterback. That gave Baltimore a one-game lead in the AFC North, but a loss to Cleveland would put the Browns back in the top spot.

Ravens coach Jesse Minter told reporters on Monday that Jackson is "definitely doing better."

Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs will be back in action after spending Week 5 on bye. They'll face a Los Angeles Chargers team that is banged-up and still searching for its first win. It might feel like an easy game for Kansas City, but divisional matchups are usually anything but.

Sunday's nightcap will pit the Dallas Cowboys against the Packers in a clash of playoff hopefuls that have stumbled through the early season. Green Bay's offense finally found a rhythm in Week 5, though, while Dallas' defense continues to stink.

The San Francisco 49ers will close out the week against a Commanders team that appears to be on the verge of imploding. While it's a mismatch on paper, San Francisco's injuries—along with Washington's desperation—could lead to a closer outcome than most expect.

articles.title: How Many Wins Remain on Cleveland Browns' 2026 NFL Schedule After Week 5 Loss?
articles.summary: A 3-1 start going into Week 5 was a real reason for optimism for the Cleveland Browns. A Week 5 loss to the New York Jets was a harsh reality check.
articles.body:
A 3-1 start going into Week 5 was a real reason for optimism for the Cleveland Browns. A Week 5 loss to the New York Jets was a harsh reality check.

The Browns have a defense that can keep them in any game from week to week. They also have an offense that can't be counted on to win games.

The first four weeks, the result was a team that could sneak into the playoffs. Week 5 looked more like a team on its way to a top-five draft pick.

The truth is probably somewhere in the middle. Let's take a look at the schedule and make week-by-week predictions to see where Cleveland could be by the end of the season.

Lamar Jackson appears to be trending in the direction of playing on Sunday. That's bad news. The Browns' offense doesn't currently inspire confidence that it can keep up.

Ravens 24, Browns 10 (Cleveland falls to 3-3)

The Titans are still in search of their first win. The Browns haven't been the kind of team that just hands those out under Monken.

Browns 17, Titans 9 (Cleveland moves to 4-3)

A shift to a heavier run script with Jaylen Warren could make this a different game in Pittsburgh. He's on fire and the Steelers put too much on Aaron Rodgers in the first meeting.

Steelers 23, Browns 20 (Cleveland falls to 4-4)

The NFC South has been good to the Browns so far. They are 2-0 against the Panthers and Bucs. Meanwhile, the Saints are just 1-4 with a middling offense and a suspect defense.

Browns 27, Saints 17 (Cleveland moves to 5-4)

A return to home against another team that is 1-4 provides another good opportunity for a win. It is a little concerning that C.J. Stroud and the defense got things rolling with a 26-3 win in Tennessee last weekend.

Texans 20, Browns 13 (Cleveland falls to 5-5)

The Raiders' 3-0 start doesn't look as great in the light of their 45-17 loss in New England last week. The schedule isn't kind to them between now and then. Expect a rested Browns team to beat Vegas for the second year in a row.

Browns 28, Raiders 17 (Cleveland moves to 6-5)

The Browns have to wait a long time to get to their first meeting with their Ohio rival this year. That might be good because it gives the defense time to continue to get better under Mike Rutenberg. The unit has held the Bengals to under 20 in their last two meetings and will give them a chance.

Browns 16, Bengals 13 (Cleveland moves to 7-5)

The Kevin Stefanski Bowl might just come down to who is starting at quarterback for the Falcons. Bijan Robinson will give the defense trouble and oft-injured Michael Penix Jr. looked good on Sunday night before suffering a rib injury.

Falcons 23, Browns 20 (Cleveland falls to 7-6)

The Giants are the NFC version of the Browns at this point. They are 3-1-1, but favorable scheduling is doing a lot of the heavy lifting in that record. Beating John Harbaugh on the road has been historically difficult for the Browns.

Giants 17, Browns 13 (Cleveland falls to 7-7)

It's going to be hard enough for the Browns to beat the Ravens at home this week and Lamar Jackson isn't even officially cleared to play. It's going to be even more difficult to win on the road in the middle of the final stretch.

Ravens 31, Browns 17 (Cleveland falls to 7-8)

How Many Wins Remain on Buffalo Bills' 2026 NFL Schedule

The final home game of the season comes against a defense that currently ranks 27th in defensive EPA per play. Indianapolis' 34-22 loss to Pittsburgh on Sunday should have the Browns feeling good about this one.

Browns 27, Colts 16 (Cleveland moves to 8-8)

Under these predictions, the Browns would enter Week 18 at 8-8, potentially still in playoff contention depending on results elsewhere. Even if a postseason berth remained within reach, though, it's hard to trust this offense to outscore the Bengals on the road.

Bengals 24, Browns 12 (Cleveland falls to 8-9)

articles.title: Week 6 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Decisions for Fantasy Football Fringe Starters
articles.summary: Week 5 was arguably the wildest week of the 2026 season so far. It began with a massive upset on the road, included several simply stunning finishes, and ended with a potential Super Bowl preview that went to overtime.
articles.body:
Week 5 was arguably the wildest week of the 2026 season so far. It began with a massive upset on the road, included several simply stunning finishes, and ended with a potential Super Bowl preview that went to overtime.

Along the way, we saw several fringe stars become difference-makers. In Monday night's game, for example, Buffalo Bills running back Ty Johnson (4 catches, 72 yards) and Los Angeles Rams tight end Tyler Higbee (5 catches, 83 yards) were two of the biggest producers on the field.

With injuries continuing to mount and the Cincinnati Bengals, Detroit Lions, Miami Dolphins, and Minnesota Vikings on bye this week, many fantasy managers will be looking for some fringe starters they can rely on, too.

Here are some early start/sit recommendations for Week 6 point-per-reception (PPR) play.

Start: MarShawn Lloyd, RB, Green Bay Packers

MarShawn Lloyd has not been particularly efficient as the Green Bay Packers' lead back in 2026. He has averaged just 2.8 yards per carry through Week 5 and has averaged a modest two receptions per game.

However, Lloyd did find the end zone twice against the Chicago Bears in Week 5, and he has another terrific matchup against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 6.

The Cowboys have surrendered six rushing touchdowns this season and have allowed an astonishing 5.1 yards per carry. They have also allowed the eighth-most fantasy points to opposing running backs.

Starting Lloyd does carry some risk, as the Packers worked in both Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong Jr. while giving Lloyd just 10 carries. However, Lloyd should see the red-zone work against a defense that can't seem to stop the run.

New York Jets running back Braelon Allen got his second start in place of the injured Breece Hall (quad) in Week 5. He rewarded fantasy managers with a tremendous game that included 16 rushing yards and a touchdown.

However, it's worth noting that Allen's breakout came against a Cleveland Browns defense that was missing its top two defensive tackles. Allen also got a heavy workload as the Browns struggled to sustain drives and put points on the board.

Allen will have a much less inviting situation this week against the New England Patriots. The Patriots can put up points in bunches, and their defense has been solid, if unspectacular. New England has allowed just 4.0 yards per carry and ranks 16th in fantasy points allowed to opposing RBs.

The fact that Allen isn't a dependable pass-catcher (3 receptions in two starts) makes this a very risky matchup.

Start: Jalen Coker, WR, Carolina Panthers

Carolina Panthers receiver Jalen Coker missed Week 4 with a quad injury, but he's trending to face the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6. Carolina was on bye last week, and head coach Dave Canales told reporters that Coker is "on track" to return.

There's no guarantee that Coker will return, of course, but managers should be prepared to put him back into their starting lineups. Bryce Young's second-favorite target was fantastic to start the season and should resume a high-volume role.

Coker caught eight of nine targets for 138 yards and two touchdowns in Week 1. He wasn't as productive in Week 2 but still finished with eight catches for 66 yards.

This week, Coker will have a favorable matchup against a struggling Philadelphia Eagles secondary. Philly has surrendered the sixth-most fantasy points to opposing wide receivers this season.

Sit: Courtland Sutton, WR, Denver Broncos

We're still waiting for Jaylen Waddle to break out in the Denver Broncos' offense. However, Waddle's presence quickly diminished the fantasy value of former No. 1 receiver Courtland Sutton.

Sutton did come through with a touchdown grab in Week 5. However, he also caught just two of three targets for 18 yards. Through five games, he's averaged just five targets, 2.2 receptions, and 20.8 yards.

After topping 1,000 yards in each of the past two seasons, Sutton has become a touchdown-dependent fantasy option. That's not what managers want to trust in a matchup with the Seattle Seahawks.

Seattle, which will visit Denver on Thursday, has surrendered six passing touchdowns this season. However, it has also surrendered the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing wide receivers.

*Fantasy scoring information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: B/R NFL Scouting Dept.'s 2027 NFL Mock Draft 1 Month Before Trade Deadline
articles.summary: The 2027 NFL draft class looks drastically different six weeks into the 2026 campaign when compared to preseason hype placed upon next year's group of talent.
articles.body:
The 2027 NFL draft class looks drastically different six weeks into the 2026 campaign when compared to preseason hype placed upon next year's group of talent.

Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith and Notre Dame cornerback Leonard Moore remain the crème de la crème. Otherwise, significant deviations took place beyond that point, specifically among the much-discussed quarterback crop.

Don't strain your eyes looking for Texas' Arch Manning, Ohio State's Julian Sayin or Notre Dame's CJ Carr. They're not included in this mock draft, because the Bleacher Report Scouting Department doesn't view them as first-round talents at this juncture. However, a pair of less-heralded transfers have worked their way up the positional hierarchy as potential top-15 draft picks.

B/R scouts Dame Parson , Brandon Thorn , Daniel Harms and Matt Holder came together to build out their latest first-round projection, break down the aforementioned quarterback setup and more.

1. Tennessee Titans: WR Jeremiah Smith, Ohio State

Team Fit : The Tennessee Titans may not know what they have in Cam Ward, but the 2025 No. 1 overall pick can certainly use more help. Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith is the consensus No. 1 overall talent for the 2027 class. He immediately becomes Tennessee's WR1 and pairs with Carnell Tate again to form a dynamic receiver duo.

Scout's Take: At wide receiver, Smith presents a near-perfect blend of size, strength and speed. He is nearly unguardable in single coverage, with the ability to beat double-coverage, too. He's an elite talent, who will elevate any passing game.

Prospects Considered : QB Drew Mestemaker, Oklahoma State; QB Darian Mensah, Miami

2. Los Angeles Chargers: CB Leonard Moore, Notre Dame

Team Fit : The Los Angeles Chargers are in the midst of a disastrous season after starting 0-5. The team could go in a myriad of directions. In this instance, the Chargers add the best cornerback prospect since Patrick Peterson. Leonard Moore can immediately replace Donte Jackson, who is a free agent next year.

Scout's Take: The class' No. 1 corner brings a great blend of size, physicality and technique. Moore can play comfortably in man or zone coverage. He's also improved as a tackler this season, making him a truly complete player and the class' second-best prospect regardless of position.

Prospects Considered : OT Jordan Seaton, LSU; Edge Colin Simmons, Texas

3. Miami Dolphins: QB Drew Mestemaker, Oklahoma State

Team Fit : Malik Willis is the Miami Dolphins' QB1 on a provisionary basis. He can keep the job if he plays well enough to warrant consideration. Through five weeks of play, the Dolphins offense is the league's worst over the last five seasons . Willis can serve as a bridge quarterback next year or be released outright to make way for the top QB prospect in the 2027 draft class.

Scout's Take: Mestemaker has arguably the best physical toolbox among next year's quarterback class. He's also a gamer. He presents the arm talent to attack the entire field when working inside and outside the pocket. Once his plus-level athleticism is added to the mix, he becomes a threat to break contain and make plays with his rushing ability.

Prospects Considered : QB Darian Mensah, Miami; OT Jordan Seaton, LSU

4. Houston Texans: OT Jordan Seaton, LSU

Team Fit : The Houston Texans' offensive line has been a major sticking point since C.J. Stroud's second year as the team's starting quarterback. The organization's decision to trade Pro Bowl left tackle Laremy Tunsil prior to the 2025 campaign certainly didn't help matters. Aireontae Ersery has proved himself as a functional starter, but Seaton is a different caliber of prospect, particularly as a pass protector.

Scout's Take: Seaton gives Houston a high-end tackle prospect with the lateral range, active hands and recovery ability to hold up on an island. He presents legitimate cornerstone traits at a premium position.

Prospects Considered : DL Will Echoles, Ole Miss; Edge Yhonzae Pierre, Alabama

5. Tampa Bay Buccaneers: Edge Colin Simmons, Texas

Team Fit : The Tampa Bay Buccaneers just selected Rueben Bain Jr. in this year's first round. However, Bain has disappointed to start his career. Colin Simmons does provide an ideal complementary skill set if/when Bain blossoms. Also, veteran edge-defender Yaya Diaby is a free agent after this season.

Scout's Take: Simmons entered the season as B/R's top edge defender, and he's currently leading the FBS with 9.5 sacks through five games. On top of his natural pass-rush skills and athleticism, the Longhorn has added an impressive up-and-under move to get after the quarterback.

Prospects Considered : DL Will Echoles, Ole Miss; Edge Dylan Stewart, South Carolina

6. Arizona Cardinals: Edge Dylan Stewart, South Carolina

Team Fit : Quarterback will certainly be at the forefront of any conversation regarding the Arizona Cardinals this coming offseason. Jacoby Brissett continues to put up numbers while the team regularly loses. Eventually, third-round rookie Carson Beck should get a look. However, the Cardinals roster isn't built to the point where this pick should be forced. Instead, Dylan Stewart provides an elite talent at a different premium position.

Scout's Take: At this point, selecting Stewart with a top-10 pick is a gamble. Between an injury and a recent suspension, he hasn't been on the field much through the first half of this season. His suspension following his on-field conduct against Alabama also raises concerns about his discipline. But the highly athletic, 6'5", 250-pound edge-defender has the best traits of any pass-rusher in the class, making him worth the bet.

Prospects Considered : QB Darian Mensah, Miami; WR Cam Coleman, Texas

7. New Orleans Saints: DL Will Echoles, Ole Miss

Team Fit : The New Orleans Saints showed significant progress toward the end of the 2025 campaign. Now at 1-4, with three straight home losses, the regression is real. Currently, the Saints are particularly bad at the point of attack. New Orleans ranks among the league's bottom three in run defense. The class' DT1 can certainly help matters.

Scout's Take: Through the first half of the college football season, Ole Miss' Will Echoles has shown why he's the draft class' best defensive tackle. He's a top-tier run defender. He has also improved as a pass-rusher, living in LSU's backfield during their Week 3 matchup.

Prospects Considered : Edge Yhonzae Pierre, Alabama; DL David Stone, Oklahoma

8. Washington Commanders: WR Charlie Becker, Indiana

Team Fit : A healthy Jayden Daniels needs weapons around him. Terry McLaurin remains a quality receiver, but he turns 32 next year. Meanwhile, Stefon Diggs and Dyami Brown aren't signed beyond this season. Indiana's Charlie Becker can provide instant offense as a legitimate deep threat. He'd also form a young and complementary duo with Antonio Williams.

Scout's Take: Becker has great size, speed and ball skills, making him an ideal perimeter threat who can take the top off defenses. The Hoosier also displays excellent body control to attack the ball and win back-shoulder fades.

Prospects Considered : WR Cam Coleman, Texas; CB Ashton Hampton, Clemson

9. New York Jets (via Dallas): QB Darian Mensah, Miami

Team Fit : Everything the New York Jets have done over the last two seasons has led to this point. Rather than continuing to rely on veteran stopgaps such as Justin Fields and Geno Smith, the franchise needs a long-term answer at quarterback. With three first-round picks in 2027, the Jets must do everything in their power to land their preferred QB prospect.

Scout's Take: Mensah is a silky smooth pocket passer. He plays with poise under pressure and navigates the pocket well. Accuracy and ball placement are his superpowers. He's tremendous at leading his receivers to open grass and away from coverage. Mensah will also stand tall in the pocket and deliver under heavy fire, displaying his toughness. While the Miami QB lacks elite physical tools, he makes up for them with a high football IQ.

Prospects Considered : QB Austin Simmons, Missouri

10. Philadelphia Eagles: IOL Anthonie Knapp, Notre Dame

Team Fit : General manager Howie Roseman has built the Philadelphia Eagles' roster through the trenches. The offensive side of the ball has taken significant hits this year due to Lane Johnson's retirement and the Cam Jurgens trade. Landon Dickerson is dealing with an injury once again. The Eagles still expect to compete at a high level, but they'll need the right building blocks in place to make that happen. Notre Dame's Anthonie Knapp is a versatile and physical option to fortify this ailing group.

Scout's Take: Knapp fits Philadelphia's desired identity up front with his play-strength, heavy hands, anchor and ability to create movement in the run game. He also has enough mobility to execute in space and gives them a potential long-term difference-maker along the interior.

Prospects Considered : Edge Yhonzae Pierre, Alabama; CB Ellis Robinson IV, Georgia

11. New York Jets: CB Ashton Hampton, Clemson

Team Fit : Once the New York Jets land their quarterback, everything beyond that point is simply icing on the cake. Clemson's Ashton Hampton adds legitimate CB1 talent into the mix, with the chance to improve yet another premium position. Furthermore, the Jets' current top corner, Brandon Stephens, turns 30 next year with no remaining guaranteed money on his contract.

Scout's Take: Hampton hasn't allowed a rocky Clemson season to derail his development. In fact, he's been one of the nation's most improved players. His length and ball tracking show up at the catch point, while his coverage versatility makes him tough to face. His aggressiveness can be taken advantage of on occasion, but that same aggression allows him to impose his will on the competition.

12. New York Jets (via Indianapolis): Edge Yhonzae Pierre, Alabama

Team Fit : The New York Jets go three-for-three in addressing premium positions. This year's second overall draft pick, David Bailey, has been outstanding at creating pressure. Trade rumors are currently circulating around fellow edge-defender Will McDonald IV. Kingsley Enagbare isn't signed beyond this season, either. Bailey needs a long-term running mate.

Scout's Take: It's hard to watch Alabama's Yhonzae Pierre play and not be overly impressed with his athletic ability. His physical traits were on display during his pick-six in Week 1. Those same natural gifts should help him develop into a productive pass-rusher at the next level.

Prospects Considered : DL David Stone, Oklahoma; LB Chris Cole, Georgia

13. Cleveland Browns (via LA Rams): QB Austin Simmons, Missouri

Team Fit : Deshaun Watson has outperformed expectations and quieted chatter about Shedeur Sanders taking over as the Cleveland Browns' QB1. Even so, Watson hasn't been particularly good. He's simply been good enough to help Cleveland establish a winning record. Besides, the veteran quarterback isn't signed beyond this season and the organization should finally move on from its mistake. Thus, quarterback remains the primary need in Cleveland. Same as it ever was.

Scout's Take: Missouri's Austin Simmons is a natural passer with near-elite arm strength to make every throw. He rips passes with immense velocity in the short-to-intermediate areas of the field. He throws a beautiful deep ball with arc and power to drop right into the bucket. He's also capable of using his legs if necessary. Overall, the 20-year-old is an ascending prospect who hasn't come close to reaching his ceiling.

Prospects Considered : QB Trinidad Chambliss, Ole Miss; QB Dante Moore, Oregon

14. Atlanta Falcons: CB Ellis Robinson IV, Georgia

Team Fit : The Atlanta Falcons field a quality run defense. The same can't be said about the team's ability to slow opposing aerial attacks. Currently, Atlanta's pass defense ranks among the league's bottom six. Granted, the Falcons' secondary is dealing with injuries. However, Georgia's Ellis Robinson IV can add another significant talent, while creating flexibility through the entire unit.

Scout's Take: As the class' best athlete among the top corners, Robinson presents immense growth potential to go with his recovery ability, ball skills and zone-coverage prowess. He's an instinctual route identifier, who's a little undersized but aggressive in his approach. The true junior prospect has taken his game to another level and shown a knack for creating takeaways.

Prospects Considered : LB Chris Cole, Georgia; QB Trinidad Chambliss, Ole Miss

15. Cincinnati Bengals: OT Trevor Goosby, Texas

Team Fit : Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow isn't taking the same kind of beating he's endured during previous seasons, which is a very good thing. However, the Bengals shouldn't be content with their current standing. The team can continue to build its offensive line and provide an impenetrable wall for its quarterback. With left tackle Orlando Brown Jr. turning 31 next year and an out existing in his contract, the Bengals can outright replace him with Texas' Trevor Goosby or groom the Longhorn to eventually take over Burrow's blind side.

Scout's Take: Goosby brings the size, length, grip-strength and anchor to grow into a reliable starter. His physical profile gives Cincinnati a high-upside answer at a premium position, especially with Brown's pass protection issues becoming more of a factor over the last couple of seasons.

Prospects Considered : CB Zabien Brown, Alabama; LB Chris Cole, Georgia

16. Pittsburgh Steelers: WR Cam Coleman, Texas

Team Fit : The Pittsburgh Steelers could enter next season with either Drew Allar or Will Howard as their starting quarterback. In particular, Allar has been a pet project for head coach Mike McCarthy, who may favor this year's third-round draft pick. At this point in the draft, Texas' Cam Coleman is a much better value to pair with DK Metcalf than forcing the class' QB4 into this slot.

Scout's Take: Coleman is a vertical, playmaking boundary wide receiver with great traits. The 20-year-old target is a one-speed route runner who separates well from man coverage. His top-end speed allows him to glide past flat-footed defenders for opportunities down the field. He also has excellent body control to serve as a significant red-zone threat.

17. Cleveland Browns: Edge Kenyatta Jackson Jr., Ohio State

Team Fit : With quarterback already addressed, the Cleveland Browns can shift their attention to another premium position. Jared Verse became the critical component to ensure the Myles Garrett trade was completed. With Isaiah McGuire set to hit free agency and Alex Wright coming off a ruptured Achilles tendon, the Browns can draft Ohio State's Kenyatta Jackson Jr. to provide Verse with an every-down bookend.

Scout's Take: Jackson's game is rooted in power, but he showed improved athleticism through the halfway point of this year's college football season. Those movement skills have appeared in his pass rush and elevated him into the first-round discussion. The Buckeye is now a more well-rounded and versatile edge-defender than previously seen.

Prospects Considered : DL David Stone, Oklahoma; CB Zabien Brown, Alabama

18. Seattle Seahawks: WR Nick Marsh, Indiana

Team Fit : Jaxon Smith-Njigba can't do it all. Or can he? The reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year has been targeted more times this season than the Seattle Seahawks' next three receivers combined. Eventually, the Seahawks must find another threat in the passing game. Indiana's Nick Marsh has a similar playing style to Cooper Kupp's, which should make his inclusion an easy transition.

Scout's Take: Marsh is a densely built and physical wide receiver. He has powerful hands and plays through the catch-point. The 6'3", 215-pound target is surprisingly quick in short areas and at the top of his routes. He's a good route-runner who creates space working against man coverage. The Michigan State transfer is also shifty after the catch to provide a well-rounded playmaker.

Prospects Considered : IOL Kade Pieper, Iowa; DL David Stone, Oklahoma

19. Carolina Panthers: TE Jamari Johnson, Oregon

Team Fit : The Carolina Panthers' Tommy Tremble and Mitchell Evans are quality tight ends. They're also better working inline than serving as targets in the passing game, hence the presence of 34-year-old veteran Darren Waller in Carolina's lineup. Oregon's Jamari Johnson provides the Panthers offense with a mismatch creator and playmaker after the catch.

Scout's Take: Johnson brings the body type and athleticism required to be a three-down threat. His ball skills and route-running nuance separate him from the pack, which should make him a quarterback's best friend. Reliable hands, the ability to identify soft spots in zone coverage and post-catch explosiveness, what's not to love?

Prospects Considered : CB Zabien Brown, Alabama; OT Trevor Lauck, Iowa

20. Las Vegas Raiders: DL David Stone, Oklahoma

Team Fit : The Las Vegas Raiders are soft at the point of attack. As a result, they're found among the league's bottom-five run defenses. The lineup's entire group of interior defenders can best be described as replacement-level players. Oklahoma's David Stone presents a different caliber of talent compared to what the Raiders currently field at the position.

Scout's Take: Stone experienced a slow start to the 2026 campaign but has been much more active against the run over the last few weeks. He's still more of a traits/toolsy prospect as a pass-rusher than a finished product, but the 6'3", 312-pound defensive tackle's combination of size, strength, length and athleticism gives him plenty of tools to become a well-rounded player at the next level.

Prospects Considered : WR Ryan Coleman-Williams, Alabama; OT Trevor Lauck, Iowa

21. Dallas Cowboys (via Green Bay): CB Zabien Brown, Alabama

Team Fit : The Dallas Cowboys still haven't figured out how to improve their defense. The unit currently ranks 31st in total defense. While Dallas just acquired Joey Porter Jr. in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers, the Cowboys' secondary requires further reinforcements. DaRon Bland is a feast-or-famine defensive back, who can be released next offseason to save $13 million with a June 1 designation. Alabama's Zabien Brown can then slot opposite JPJ.

Scout's Take: Brown comes to play when the lights get bright and his instincts can take over. He has ideal size and length working on the perimeter and won't back down to any assignment. At this stage in his career, he's better in zone coverage than man but has the length and athleticism to develop further. While Brown didn't have his best showing against the Georgia Bulldogs, expect him to bounce back as an impact defender.

Prospects Considered : WR Ryan Coleman-Williams, Alabama; S Brauntae Johnson, Notre Dame

22. Denver Broncos: RB Jadan Baugh, Florida

Team Fit : The Denver Broncos' offensive inadequacies continue unabated—so much so that head coach Sean Payton took play-calling duties away from offensive coordinator Davis Webb. A more consistent run game could help the team get off to better starts and take pressure off of quarterback Bo Nix. Florida's Jadan Baugh is the class' RB1 with a complete skill set as an every-down back.

Scout's Take: Baugh is a compact and densely built running back with a mean stiff-arm. He's a bell-cow back, who gets stronger as his touches accumulate. The Florida ball-carrier is a fleet-footed mover with open-field elusiveness to force missed tackles. Baugh will also finish runs downhill with a forward lean, making him a good short-yardage option. He can then be deployed out of the backfield as a legitimate threat in the passing game.

Prospects Considered : Edge Boubacar Traore, Notre Dame; TE Trey'Dez Green, LSU

23. Chicago Bears: OT Trevor Lauck, Iowa

Team Fit : The Chicago Bears' coaching staff rotated its left tackles until Braxton Jones suffered an injury. Throw Ozzy Trapilo and Theo Benedet into the mix. It doesn't matter. None of them are the answer to protect Caleb Williams' blind side. Meanwhile, the Iowa Hawkeyes have long served as an assembly line of NFL blockers.

Scout's Take: Trevor Lauck is a powerful, technically sound blocker with strong hands, a stout anchor and real displacement ability in the run game. Even if he ultimately ends up working inside as a guard, his strength and tackle experience give Chicago valuable flexibility.

Prospects Considered : Edge Boubacar Traore, Notre Dame; S Brauntae Johnson, Notre Dame

24. New England Patriots: WR Ryan Coleman-Williams, Alabama

Team Fit : Wide receivers A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs joined the New England Patriots this year. The organization shouldn't stop there. The franchise is now built around Drake Maye. Added talent around the quarterback position should be a priority. Alabama's Ryan Coleman-Williams has experienced concentration drops throughout his career, but he appears to have put it all together over the last five weeks.

Scout's Take: Coleman-Williams is a dynamic playmaker. He has good football IQ and coverage recognition to attack man and zone coverages post-snap. The former 5-star recruit presents excellent top-end speed, making him an explosive run-after-catch threat. As long as Coleman-Williams keeps the concentration drops under control, he presents as much upside as any wide receiver in the class not named Jeremiah Smith.

Prospects Considered : CB Jyaire Hill, Michigan; DL A'Mauri Washington, Oregon

25. Detroit Lions: CB Jyaire Hill, Michigan

Team Fit : The Detroit Lions' pass defense is awful. The unit currently ranks dead last and allows nearly 300 yards per game. The Lions should clean house at cornerback once this season is over and bring in Michigan's Jyaire Hill to start over at the premium position. Detroit's offense is far too good to be held back by a defense that struggles to slow anyone.

Scout's Take: Hill is an incredibly toolsy prospect with man and zone versatility, a unique size/athleticism profile and physicality that will occasionally get him into trouble. His route-recognition and ball skills are obvious. Plus, he can be weaponized by sending him on blitzes. Hill loves blowing up plays behind the line of scrimmage and presents significant growth potential.

Prospects Considered : CB Kelley Jones, Mississippi State; TE Trey'Dez Green, LSU

26. New York Giants: DL A'Mauri Washington, Oregon

Team Fit : The New York Giants already feature significant talent among their defensive front seven. However, the team's decision to trade Dexter Lawrence this offseason left the team without a massive and athletic tone-setter along the interior. Currently, the Giants rank among the league's bottom eight in run defense and allow nearly 130 yards per contest. Oregon's A'Mauri Washington has the type of athletic traits that profile similarly to Lawrence.

Scout's Take: Washington hasn't taken the next step this fall. However, his floor projects as a good run-defender who can play from multiple alignments. While the 6'3", 320-pound defensive tackle may not win frequently enough as a pass-rusher, he can impact the passing game with how good he is at batting passes at the line of scrimmage.

Prospects Considered : IOL Kade Pieper, Iowa; CB Kelley Jones, Mississippi State

27. Jacksonville Jaguars: Edge Boubacar Traore, Notre Dame

Team Fit : The Jacksonville Jaguars' offense is capable of building early leads and requires a complementary defense to harass trailing opponents. The addition of another edge-rusher may come across as counterintuitive after the franchise's investments in Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker. However, Walker can be a wrecking ball when reduced down over guards in sub-packages, while Notre Dame's Boubacar Traore provides another explosive, upfield edge-rusher.

Scout's Take: Don't expect Traore to be a complete defender or a factor against the run at the onset of his NFL career. But the Golden Domer is a very good athlete with a nasty spin-move that will help him constantly put pressure on opposing quarterbacks.

Prospects Considered : LB Chris Cole, Georgia; OT Lance Heard, Kentucky

28. Buffalo Bills: S Brauntae Johnson, Notre Dame

Team Fit : The Buffalo Bills haven't quite figured out the safety position since moving on from their longtime tandem of Jordan Poyer and Micah Hyde. Cole Bishop is only 23, but he's an inconsistent tackler. C.J. Gardner-Johnson and rookie Jalon Kilgore are better suited playing over the slot. By contrast, Notre Dame's Brauntae Johnson is a complete option.

Scout's Take: Physicality and size in the run game, paired with instinctual play on the back end, make Johnson a true impact playmaker. While an injury has limited Johnson this season, his unique blend of movement skills, raw talent and leadership has been noticeable throughout his collegiate career. Those same traits will help any NFL secondary.

Prospects Considered : WR Reed Harris, Arizona State; DL Matayo Uiagalelei, Oregon

29. Baltimore Ravens: WR Deuce Alexander, Ole Miss

Team Fit : Zay Flowers has been outstanding since signing a four-year, $140 million contract extension this past August. Flowers leads the Baltimore Ravens with 433 receiving yards. Conversely, Rashod Bateman doesn't provide enough as the team's WR2. Instead, Baltimore adds a more dynamic option to help quarterback Lamar Jackson and take pressure off the team's run game.

Scout's Take: Ole Miss' Deuce Alexander is an explosive wide receiver and a dangerous threat after the catch. He has great speed to beat defenders vertically to create chunk plays. The junior prospect is also a good route-runner, who decelerates and accelerates well to keep defenders off-balance.

Prospects Considered : DL Justin Scott, Miami; RB Kewan Lacy, Ole Miss

30. Minnesota Vikings: QB Dante Moore, Oregon

Team Fit : Kyler Murray could earn a contract extension this offseason depending on how the Minnesota Vikings finish the campaign. Murray has transitioned well into Kevin O'Connell's scheme, while the coach continues to implement plays that help accentuate the quarterback's strengths. Even if Murray does re-sign, Oregon's Dante Moore isn't unfamiliar with sitting for a year, and the Vikings could have a succession plan in place after their last attempt went awry.

Scout's Take: Moore is an accurate and poised quarterback with good size and enough arm talent to throw with velocity and touch. The 21-year-old must improve his pocket toughness when pressured and perform at a higher level against top competition. Still, his upside remains an intriguing option, especially late in the first round.

Prospects Considered : Edge Will Heldt, Clemson; RB Kewan Lacy, Ole Miss

31. Kansas City Chiefs: TE Trey'Dez Green, LSU

Team Fit : Travis Kelce continues to be the Kansas City Chiefs' No. 1 target, even at 37 years old. Why wait until the future Hall of Famer has nothing left? Or Kelce could realistically walk away from the game this offseason. With or without the franchise's all-time leading receiver, the Chiefs can grab another weapon at tight end to maintain the team's offensive standard and keep quarterback Patrick Mahomes happy.

Scout's Take: Next year's tight end class features some imposing prospects. At a listed 6'7" and 240 pounds, LSU's Trey'Dez Green is one of the most noticeable. The 20-year-old prospect is still learning the nuances of the position, but he's a problem down the seam and creates after the catch. Plus, Green has already shown improvement as a blocker.

Prospects Considered : OT Lance Heard, Kentucky; LB Chris Cole, Georgia

32. San Francisco 49ers: IOL Kade Pieper, Iowa

Team Fit : The San Francisco 49ers are a well-coached team with talent at every level. Specifically, the squad's preparation and structure allow the Niners to overcome deficiencies. Right now, San Francisco's offensive interior isn't a strong point. Upgrades should be considered. Iowa's Kade Pieper can come in and start over Connor Colby at left guard or transition to center and replace the 34-year-old Jake Brendel, who's in the last year of his current deal.

Scout's Take: Pieper's explosiveness, lateral quickness and ability to cover ground make him a natural fit for San Francisco's movement-heavy run game. He needs more mass and play-strength, but his athleticism and potential center flexibility give him a strong developmental ceiling.

Prospects Considered : LB Chris Cole, Georgia; S KJ Bolden, Georgia
