articles.summary: The 4-1 Buffalo Bills wrap up the first segment of their 2026 schedule when they face the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday in Nevada.
articles.body:
The 4-1 Buffalo Bills wrap up the first segment of their 2026 schedule when they face the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday in Nevada.

After that, they'll enjoy a bye week before embarking on the middle portion of the schedule with a potentially crucial home game against the Baltimore Ravens on Nov. 1.

Let's look at those matchups as well as the rest of the remaining slate to identify where Buffalo might stumble and make some predictions for how things will play out for Josh Allen and Co. between now and January.

The Bills have to be careful here. This is a potential trap for a team that remains on the road on short rest following an energy-sapping overtime win over the Rams in Los Angeles. That said, the Raiders' defense was exposed by New England and I think these teams are moving in very different directions. I'm expecting Buffalo to pull through.

Bills 27, Raiders 20 (Buffalo moves to 5-1)

This won't be easy, especially if Lamar Jackson is 100 percent at this point. That said, the Bills will have had two weeks to prepare for a home game against a clearly flawed rival whose number they've had in recent years. This is the right place and right time for Buffalo.

Bills 30, Ravens 24 (Buffalo moves to 6-1)

The Bills tend to lay an egg a couple of times per season. This spot makes a lot of sense as they go on the road to play a balanced, well-coached team with offensive weapons that are likely to present major challenges to Buffalo's problematic second and third levels.

Vikings 28, Bills 24 (Buffalo falls to 6-2)

The Bills are too talented, experienced and mentally tough to drop both games on this mini road trip. They've outscored the Jets 105-32 in their last three meetings and have won five straight matchups with Gang Green. This shouldn't be close, but it's still a divisional road game, so Buffalo needs to stay focused.

Bills 35, Jets 17 (Buffalo moves to 7-2)

Miami beat the Bills last November, but this is a very different Dolphins team. Thus far, it hasn't looked like one that is NFL-caliber, especially away from home. This is a tough spot for a Miami team that has managed just three touchdowns in three road games this year and will be coming off another away contest in Indianapolis.

Bills 34, Dolphins 13 (Buffalo moves to 8-2)

Obviously, this is somewhat of a toss-up considering their history and the fact that both teams are prime contenders. But the Bills are lucky to get the juggernaut Chiefs at home, with Kansas City traveling on short rest for a Thanksgiving Thursday nighter. I expect this to be a memorable Bills victory at the new Highmark Stadium.

Bills 30, Chiefs 28 (Buffalo moves to 9-2)

The Patriots have a later bye and could be fresher for this home game, but the Bills also benefit from extra rest following the Thursday matchup with Kansas City while the Pats are flying back from Los Angeles. Ultimately, I think the Bills find a way to split the season series and beat the Pats in December for a seventh consecutive year (with five of those coming in Foxborough).

Bills 27, Patriots 24 (Buffalo moves to 10-2)

I had them splitting a mini road trip to Minnesota and New York in November, and this mini trip through New England and Green Bay makes sense as another 1-1 split. This is a tough prime-time spot at Lambeau after a potentially taxing win at Gillette Stadium. But if they lose to the Patriots, I can see them rallying for the W in this situation. Regardless, it leaves them with a 10-3 record entering the holiday home stretch.

Packers 28, Bills 24 (Buffalo falls to 10-3)

This is the back half of a two-game road swing for the Bears, who may lack what it takes to slow down the Buffalo offense in prime time at Highmark on short rest.

Bills 30, Bears 20 (Buffalo moves to 11-3)

This is definitely a winnable game for the Bills, but few would fault them for falling in this road spot on short rest against a very talented and potentially desperate opponent.

Broncos 24, Bills 21 (Buffalo falls to 11-4)

How Many Wins Remain on Cleveland Browns' 2026 NFL Schedule

This might be one to be wary of. The Dolphins could have a lot more figured out by this point; it's their second home game in a row, and they did crush the Bills 30-13 at this site last November. If Buffalo does come up short in Denver, it will get its act together here. If the Bills beat the Broncos, this might be a trap. Regardless, I've got them pegged for 12 wins entering the final week of the season.

Bills 30, Dolphins 27 (Buffalo moves to 12-4)

This is likely only a defeat if it doesn't matter, which is unlikely considering that I've given them four losses. That should keep them within striking distance of the AFC's top seed while keeping New England close enough in the rear-view mirror to force Buffalo to take care of business at home against a team that they've dominated in recent seasons.

Bills 27, Jets 17 (Buffalo finishes 13-4)

I'm projecting nine more wins over Buffalo's final 12 games, resulting in a 13-4 finish.

articles.title: Week 6 Waiver Wire Top Pickups and Drops After Evaluating Week 5 Box Scores
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL season has been a tricky one to navigate for fantasy managers. Injuries have been a significant and persistent part of the equation, and we saw more players go down in Week 5.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL season has been a tricky one to navigate for fantasy managers. Injuries have been a significant and persistent part of the equation, and we saw more players go down in Week 5.

The list of players who suffered injuries over the weekend includes David Montgomery, Deebo Samuel, Roman Wilson, and Michael Penix Jr.

Byes are also part of the picture at this point in the season. This week, the Cincinnati Bengals, Detroit Lions, Miami Dolphins, and Minnesota Vikings will be off. Naturally, managers will be looking to backfill lineups with sleepers off the waiver wire.

Here, you'll find a look at some of the top pickups and drops for Week 6, based on recent production, projected roles, and point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

The Las Vegas Raiders finally turned to rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza this past week. However, they did so because of the score and not because of Kirk Cousins' performance.

Cousins has been a steady signal-caller for the Raiders, and he's been a solid streamer in fantasy. He has topped 20 points in three of his five outings and has another strong matchup this week.

Las Vegas will host the Buffalo Bills, who have surrendered the fourth-most fantasy points to opposing QBs. Cousins is still only rostered in 45 percent of leagues.

While Cousins has been steady, Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix has not. The offseason addition of Jaylen Waddle has not elevated his fantasy floor as many might have hoped, and last week's change in play-calling didn't help either.

Sean Payton took play-calling away from offensive coordinator Davis Webb ahead of Week 5.

Nix and the entire Broncos offense have been disjointed all season, and the third-year signal-caller has only reached 20 points once. He's not trustworthy, and he certainly can't be trusted against a stout Seattle Seahawks defense this week.

There's a chance that Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley will return from his hamstring injury this week. Coach Nick Sirianni told reporters that he's "hopeful" that Barkley and DeVonta Smith will return for Week 6, per ESPN's Tim McManus.

With Barkley's status still uncertain, though, Dameon Pierce is a strong add for the week. Tank Bigsby is on injured reserve, while Will Shipley suffered a foot injury on Sunday, leaving Pierce as the last healthy option.

This week, the Eagles will host a Carolina Panthers team that has surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing RBs. He's rostered in only two percent of leagues.

Drop: Kenneth Gainwell, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

When the season started, it certainly felt like Kenneth Gainwell could be a high-end complement to Bucky Irving for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. For whatever reason, though, he simply hasn't become a big part of Zac Robinson's offense.

Tampa leaned on the run heavily in Week 5, but Gainwell (four carries) was firmly behind both Irving (21) and Sean Tucker (5) in the running rotation. Gainwell did have three catches, but a limited receiving role isn't enough to make him a dependable option, even in PPR.

On Sunday, the Arizona Cardinals agreed to trade wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans. With Harrison out, Kendrick Bourne becomes the new No. 2 receiver opposite Michael Wilson.

While Bourne won't have an extremely favorable matchup this week against the Los Angeles Rams, his workload should pull him through for fantasy managers. On Sunday, he caught five of eight targets for 70 yards.

Bourne is rostered in just three percent of fantasy leagues.

Drop: Brian Thomas Jr., Jacksonville Jaguars

The Jacksonville Jaguars haven't traded wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. yet, but they may consider it before the November 10 deadline. That's how far out of the game plan the 2024 first-round pick has fallen.

Thomas caught a touchdown pass in Week 4, but he has just nine catches for 109 yards on 18 targets this season. 80 of those yards came in the first two weeks, and Thomas hasn't reached 20 yards in a game since.

It's simply not worth keeping Thomas in the hope that something changes.

articles.title: 2026 NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 6
articles.summary: Another big NFL trade domino dropped over the weekend, as the Arizona Cardinals sent wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans. We've now seen a handful of blockbuster in-season deals in 2026, and the trade deadline is still nearly a month away.
articles.body:
Another big NFL trade domino dropped over the weekend, as the Arizona Cardinals sent wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans. We've now seen a handful of blockbuster in-season deals in 2026, and the trade deadline is still nearly a month away.

Teams have until 4 p.m. ET on November 10 to make deals.

The trade market is already picking up—we also saw the Philadelphia Eagles deal Cam Jurgens last week—and the deals are likely to come in more frequently from here. No team has been mathematically eliminated yet, but three sit at 0-5, a mark from which no franchise has ever made the playoffs.

Here, you'll find an updated look at our top 10 trade candidates, ranked according to factors like past production, upside, positional value, contract/cap implications, projected availability, and any relevant recent rumors.

You'll also find projected trade values based on factors such as position, player upside, player age, and any comparable deals, along with some logical suitors for each player.

10. Donte Jackson, CB, Los Angeles Chargers

Projected Trade Value: 2027 5th-Round Pick

Donte Jackson resides at the bottom of our list because of his health. He's battling a hamstring injury and missed Week 5. He's currently considered week-to-week, according to ESPN's Anthony Gharib .

Teams may not be eager to make a move for Jackson until he's clearly healthy, but he's a player worth targeting before November 10.

The Los Angeles Chargers appear to be going nowhere this season after a 0-5 start and numerous injuries across the roster. Jackson, meanwhile, plays an in-demand position and is set to be a free agent in 2027—trading him would save L.A. $6 million in 2026 cap space.

Jackson started 15 games for the Chargers last season and allowed an opposing passer rating of only 56.8 in coverage. Now that the Pittsburgh Steelers have dealt Joey Porter Jr., Jackson should be a top option for cornerback-needy teams.

Potential Suitors: Buffalo Bills, Carolina Panthers

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 5th-Round Pick

The 0-5 Tennessee Titans are in just as much trouble as the winless Chargers, perhaps even more. While Los Angeles' season has certainly been a disappointment, the Titans have seemed unable to improve for multiple seasons.

More alarmingly, second-year quarterback Cam Ward doesn't appear to be showing the development expected of a former No. 1 overall pick.

Tennessee isn't going to the playoffs this season, and it should be focused on getting more out of Ward before the end of the year. While keeping starting running back Tony Pollard would help support Ward, though, it may be time to move him.

The Titans are playing for their future, and the 29-year-old isn't likely to be a part of it. He's set to be a free agent in the spring, and trading him would save $7.3 million in cap space.

Trading Pollard would also likely bring back additional draft capital. A long list of backfield injuries grew in Week 5, as players like TreVeyon Henderson, Quinshon Judkins, and Will Shipley joined it.

Potential Suitors: Cleveland Browns, Green Bay Packers

8. Mason Rudolph, QB, Pittsburgh Steelers

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 6th-Round Pick

San Francisco 49ers quarterback Mac Jones lingered on our list for some time because of his status as a top backup and a 2027 free agent. As injuries continue to mount in San Francisco, though, the 49ers become less likely to move their most important depth piece.

Pittsburgh Steelers backup Mason Rudolph, on the other hand, should be available to teams that need backup help. The Steelers kept four quarterbacks on their 53-man roster, with Rudolph, Will Howard, and rookie Drew Allar sitting behind Aaron Rodgers.

It's highly unlikely that Pittsburgh's plan was to keep all four quarterbacks through the trade deadline. In fact, Jason La Canfora of Casino.org reported at the start of the season that the Steelers probably would have dealt Rudolph if there was a stronger quarterback market.

Rudolph won't be valued as a starter the way Jones might be. However, he has 20 career starts (including playoffs) on his resume and should appeal to teams with questionable QB depth.

Potential Suitors: Atlanta Falcons, Washington Commanders

7. Kenneth Gainwell, RB, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Given the aforementioned cascade of 2026 running-back injuries, there should be a fair amount of interest in Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Kenneth Gainwell. The former Eagles and Steelers backup has long been a capable change-of-pace option.

Gainwell showed last season that he can be a high-volume complementary back, too. While working in tandem with Steelers starter Jaylen Warren, he racked up 187 touches, 1,023 scrimmage yards, and eight touchdowns.

The Bucs signed Gainwell to a two-year, $14 million deal, hoping to form a dangerous tandem with him and Bucky Irving. However, Gainwell simply hasn't carved out a significant role in Zac Robinson's offense.

Tampa leaned heavily on its ground game against the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday night. Irving unsurprisingly led the charge, but Gainwell saw fewer carries (four) than even Sean Tucker (five). The Buccaneers could probably be convinced to move Gainwell for a reasonable return and $2 million in 2026 cap savings.

Potential Suitors: New England Patriots, Philadelphia Eagles

The Cleveland Browns may not be as eager to move off of receiver Jerry Jeudy after promising rookie KC Concepcion suffered a concussion in Sunday's loss to the New York Jets. However, Concepcion and fellow rookie Denzel Boston still represent the future at receiver for Cleveland.

According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz , it's "pretty well known around the league" that Jeudy is available. Per Schultz, the Browns would prefer to get a third- or fourth-round pick in exchange for the receiver, though that may be difficult.

The 27-year-old struggled through last season and has fallen out of the game plan this year as Concepcion, Boston, and tight end Harold Fannin Jr. have become the go-to targets.

Still, Jeudy is a talented pass-catcher who made the Pro Bowl just two years ago following a 1,229-yard season. His skill set hasn't disappeared, and his 2026 base salary of $1.5 million should appeal to budget-conscious teams.

Potential Suitors: Kansas City Chiefs, Philadelphia Eagles

5. Brian Thomas Jr., WR, Jacksonville Jaguars

Projected Trade Value: 2027 2nd- and 6th-Round Picks

Unlike some other teams on this list, the Jacksonville Jaguars are not struggling. On the contrary, they're sitting at 4-1 with a fairly solid grip on the AFC South.

In his Substack publication The Sweep , NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported that the Jaguars have also shown "no interest" in trading wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr.

However, the return that Arizona got for Harrison could change Jacksonville's stance. Thomas was a revelation for the Jaguars as a rookie but has steadily fallen out of the game plan since.

This season, the 2024 first-rounder has caught just nine passes for 105 yards and a touchdown. With rookie receiver Josh Cameron (117 yards, 2 TDs) beginning to gain traction, cashing in Thomas now could make a ton of sense.

The Jags would undoubtedly ask for a similar return to what the Cardinals got for Harrison, and they might just get it. Thomas is still only 24 years old, and he racked up 1,282 yards with 10 touchdowns during his inaugural campaign.

Potential Suitors: Las Vegas Raiders, San Francisco 49ers

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 4th-Round Pick

During the offseason, there was some trade chatter surrounding Cardinals pass-rusher Josh Sweat. However, general manager Monti Ossenfort made it clear in August that he had no plans to move the talented defender.

"We're excited to have him, but some of those discussions are going to keep private, but excited to have Josh here. Had a great year last year. Excited for more good things out of him this year," Ossenfort said, per ESPN's Josh Weinfuss .

Of course, Ossenfort made that statement long before the Cardinals opened the season 1-4 and he decided to trade Harrison. Arizona's willingness to trade Harrison makes it reasonable to question whether its stance on Sweat could also change.

The 29-year-old is signed through 2028 but looms as a potential 2027 cap casualty. The Cardinals could release him with a post-June 1 designation in the spring and save $18.1 million in cap space. It could make more sense to trade Sweat, who had 12 sacks last season, well ahead of 2027.

Potential Suitors: Chicago Bears, Green Bay Packers

3. Landon Dickerson, G, Philadelphia Eagles

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 2nd-Round Pick

Starting Eagles guard Landon Dickerson is certainly a surprise new addition to our board. However, Philly's decision to trade Jurgens also came as a surprise. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , some around the league believe that Howie Roseman isn't finished moving pieces:

"Accordingly, it would not surprise those in the league if teams start calling on Eagles guard Landon Dickerson when he is healthy enough to return from injured reserve."

Dickerson has been out since he tried to play through a knee injury in Week 1 but landed on injured reserve. He's one of the league's top interior linemen when healthy, and the Eagles certainly won't part with him for proverbial pennies. However, if the buzz indicates that Dickerson could be available, guard-needy teams should be placing calls.

The three-time Pro Bowler just turned 28 years old, and he's under contract through 2028.

Potential Suitors: Cleveland Browns, San Francisco 49ers

The Miami Dolphins remain winless. While they've looked like a scrappy young team that might steal a few victories late in the season, it's been clear since the summer that they are building for 2027 and beyond.

Miami parted with several of its most notable veterans in the offseason, including standout receiver Jaylen Waddle. While the Dolphins don't have many sensible assets left to trade, veteran edge Josh Uche is an option.

Uche just turned 28 in September, but he's set to be a free agent in the spring and may not be in Miami's long-term plans. However, he's a talented rotational defender who would interest teams that need help rushing the passer.

Pro Football Focus has graded Uche as the league's 33rd-best edge-defender through Week 5. While he has logged just a single sack this season, he has added 20 tackles, a forced fumble, a fumble recovery, and four QB pressures.

1. Khalil Mack, Edge, Los Angeles Chargers

Chargers pass-rusher Khalil Mack retains the top spot on our list, which should surprise no one. Los Angeles fell to 0-5 on Sunday, while Mack continues to be a legitimate difference-maker.

Mack has logged three sacks, 15 tackles, five tackles for loss, and 10 quarterback pressures. He's also playing on a one-year deal and should be interested in playing for a team that could get him his first career playoff win.

According to The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , at least two league executives have put Mack's value at a fifth-round draft pick. While that's not an unreasonable price point, the Chargers would likely ask for more—especially considering Jaelan Phillips commanded a third-round pick at last year's trade deadline.

Yes, Phillips (27 years old) is considerably younger than the 35-year-old Mack, but he was also in the final year of his contract when he was dealt.

Mack should be the top target for any team with Super Bowl aspirations that happens to need help rushing opposing passers. It'll be a fairly significant surprise if he remains in Los Angeles beyond next month's deadline.

Potential Suitors: Chicago Bears, San Francisco 49ers

*Contract and cap information via Spotrac . Advanced statistics from Pro Football Reference unless otherwise noted.

articles.title: New Raiders Rumors on Kirk Cousins' Hot Seat as QB1 After Fernando Mendoza's Debut vs. Patriots
articles.summary: While Fernando Mendoza got his first NFL snaps in a Week 5 loss to the New England Patriots, don't expect to see the rookie assume the starting quarterback job imminently.
articles.body:
While Fernando Mendoza got his first NFL snaps in a Week 5 loss to the New England Patriots, don't expect to see the rookie assume the starting quarterback job imminently.

ESPN's Dan Graziano reported Wednesday that "Kirk Cousins is in no danger of being benched any time soon."

"The Raiders were happy to get Mendoza's feet wet, but they remain in no hurry to make him their starter, especially sitting at 3-2 themselves," the NFL insider said.

Getting blown out by New England at least afforded the opportunity to hand Mendoza his debut. He entered with Las Vegas trailing 45-17 and went 6-of-8 for 48 yards.

The cameo wasn't all that revealing. The No. 1 overall pick only got one drive, which ended in a turnover on downs, and he was mostly fine without turning any heads.

More than anything, the QB change was a reminder that Mendoza is waiting in the wings.

The Raiders aren't going to bench Cousins as long as they're winning, and his numbers have been pretty strong. He has thrown for 1,269 yards, 12 touchdowns and four interceptions. His 64.8 QBR ranks 12th among qualified passers, per ESPN.com .

Las Vegas has dropped two games in a row, though, and a difficult stretch lies ahead. Five of its next seven games prior to a Week 13 bye come against playoff teams from a season ago.

Should the Raiders start to fall out of the AFC playoff race, they'll have less reason to stick with a stopgap solution at quarterback.

articles.title: NFL Power Rankings entering Week 6: Someone has to win NFC East among disappointing Cowboys, Commanders, Giants and Eagles
articles.summary: The entire NFC East had a miserable Week 5. But someone has to win that division, even if none those teams are good.
articles.body:
NFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | Commanders NFC North : Bears | Lions | Packers | Vikings NFC South: Falcons | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers NFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | Seahawks

AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | Jets AFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | Steelers AFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars | Titans AFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers

The NFC East has become the new NFC South, at least through five games. It is the worst division in football, at least from one measure. And the eye test.

The NFC East, which has just one team over .500, is the only division in which every team ranks 20th or worse in DVOA . The Dallas Cowboys are 20th, and that's the best standing among the teams. The Philadelphia Eagles are 23rd, the New York Giants are 27th despite being 3-1-1 and the Washington Commanders are 28th. That's a lot of bad football.

The oft-told joke from Sunday was that all four NFC East teams played in Week 5, including two against each other, and the division still went winless. That's because the Giants and Commanders tied, which everyone knows because of a management mistake at the end of the game by Washington that was hard to believe . But that's the NFC East.

The rules state the division has to send a team to the playoffs. It's tough to figure out which one it could be.

The Giants have the lead but over the last three weeks they have barely beaten the Titans and Cardinals, and tied the Commanders. Those three teams are a combined 2-12-1. Jameis Winston is fun and he played well Sunday but it seems hard to believe he doesn't blow up or that the Giants stay on top. But who's going to catch them? The Eagles' best game of the season was a loss on Sunday to the Jaguars, one that rivaled the Commanders for worst late-game management by a coaching staff.

Philadelphia's only two wins are near misses against the Commanders and Titans, who are a combined 1-8-1. The Commanders might have been a reasonable answer with a win on Sunday, but they blew the chance for that and the way the game ended could linger. Even if that isn't the reason Washington fades, the Commanders' shoddy defense might be.

That leaves the Cowboys. They are the highest ranked team in DVOA. The defense is really bad, ranking 32nd. But their offense is probably the best unit in the division, except the times it goes strangely quiet, like it did last Thursday night against the Buccaneers. Still, even with that strangely lethargic loss to the Buccaneers at home, it's easier to see Dallas turning things around than any of the other three teams.

None of the four teams look like they will end up deserving a postseason spot. There's a chance the winner of the division finishes under .500 like last season's NFC South, though there will be plenty of opportunities against bad opponents when they play intradivision games.

Someone will win the NFC East. Maybe it's the Cowboys. Or, based on the way they've all played this season, it might not really matter that much.

Here are the NFL power rankings after Week 5 of the NFL season:

The good news for the Dolphins is they won't lose in Week 6. They have a bye. Good for the Dolphins to lose by only seven points against the Bengals on Sunday, but the true story of the game was a 28-10 deficit after three quarters. The Dolphins have trailed by at least 14 points in four of five games.

There are two main goals after the bye: getting one win to avoid the 0-17 questions, and finding out if Malik Willis can be the quarterback of the future. A decision in the 2027 NFL Draft looms. Willis was 1-for-7 passing for 22 yards with a minute to go in the first half Sunday. He threw two interceptions and lost a fumble. It wasn't good enough, and garbage-time stats don't fix that. Of 32 qualified quarterbacks he's 30th in adjusted EPA ( expected points added ) per play and 29th in success rate. It is hard to judge Willis fairly because there's not much talent around him, but he has to prove he can elevate his teammates.

"I will say this: We will need more consistency in our pass game in general for all 11 players to be better in order for us to take the next step," Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said .

Five games into Cam Ward's second season, the questions about benching him are starting.

"Cam is our starting quarterback," Titans head coach Robert Saleh said, according to the Associated Press . "We're going to give him every opportunity to be successful this year. We're going to continue working with him, grinding with him, and trying to help him get better."

Ward had just 170 yards on 36 pass attempts against the Texans. The Titans scored only three points. Tennessee is 3-19 in Ward's starts. He has 896 yards and three touchdowns in five starts this season. The Titans have to see it through with last year's No. 1 overall draft pick, but it doesn't look good so far this season.

The Chargers' starting offensive line on Sunday was impossibly desperate for Week 5 of an NFL season, or really any week of any season:

Left tackle: rookie fourth-round pick Travis Burke

Left guard: rookie sixth-round pick Logan Taylor

Center: rookie second-round pick Jake Slaughter

Right guard: Cole Strange, ranked 73rd of 75 guards in PFF grades

Right tackle: rookie sixth-round pick Alex Harkey

If the Chargers' situation seems beyond repair, it is. They were a bad team even when healthy, and they had numerous injuries to key players on Sunday. Justin Herbert has not played well at all, but against the Broncos it was hard to put all the blame on him considering the catastrophe of the line protecting him. It's hard to believe the Chargers' season is over — no 0-5 team has ever made the playoffs — but it's probably going to get worse before it gets better.

Trading Marvin Harrison Jr. was best for everyone involved, but let's not celebrate the Cardinals too much for getting a second-round pick back in a trade with the Texans. Arizona got very little out of the fourth overall pick in a loaded 2024 NFL Draft. That's horrendous, even if the Cardinals recouped some value. As Bob McManaman of the Arizona Republic pointed out , the Cardinals have already moved on from four of the last six players they drafted in the top 10 overall: Josh Rosen, Kyler Murray, Isaiah Simmons and Harrison.

On Sunday, the Cardinals got shredded by the Lions' offense, and Arizona's offense did surprisingly little against a bad Detroit defense before some garbage-time yards and points. It's looking bleak in Arizona, as it usually does with this franchise.

It's time to give up on the Saints until they show they're a good team. They're now 30th in DVOA, ahead of only the Titans and Dolphins. New Orleans would be 0-5 if not for a second-half rally at Baltimore, which included a go-ahead touchdown on a controversial call . It looks now like the Saints got hot against a very soft second-half schedule last season and that momentum has not carried over.

The Saints, and particularly QB Tyler Shough, were dreadful against the blitz-happy Vikings. Shough had 96 yards, two interceptions and a 38.1 passer rating. Minnesota is a tough matchup but that's bad. The Saints had 142 yards as a team. They have some winnable games coming up (at Giants, vs. Steelers, vs. Browns, vs. Panthers) but they haven't shown they're better than any of those teams.

The Jets figured out they should just get the ball to Garrett Wilson and watch good things happen. Wilson had 104 yards and a touchdown in a 17-12 win over the Browns . Wilson, who had seven catches, was targeted 11 times and no other Jet had more than four.

New York also leaned on its defense, a unit that had eight sacks and held Cleveland to a season-low 198 yards.

Wilson disappeared last season with injuries and a bad quarterback situation holding him back. He had 395 yards in seven games last year. This season he already has 374 yards and the Jets seem committed to running the offense through him.

"He's Garrett Wilson, and we think he can do that every single week," Jets quarterback Geno Smith told the media after the game . "He loves competing, he's a proven player. He makes plays when the ball comes his way. We've got to continue to find ways to get him the football, and once the ball is in his hands he'll make plays."

One win changed the Buccaneers' outlook this season. Tampa Bay looked good in beating Dallas, with rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels playing well. Even though Baker Mayfield wants to return from a dislocated thumb in Week 6, via James Palmer of Amazon Prime Video , Daniels' play makes Tampa Bay less desperate to bring back its quarterback too soon.

The NFC South doesn't have a team over .500 so it's not like the Buccaneers are out of anything, even at 1-4. Tampa Bay hosts Pittsburgh in Week 6 and then faces Carolina and then Atlanta in a two-game stretch that could revive its season.

25. Washington Commanders (1-3-1, LW: 25)

Let's wait a moment to pile on Dan Quinn, Jayden Daniels and whoever else was responsible for the fiasco at the end of Sunday's tie. There were other issues. The Commanders allowed a field goal and three touchdowns on the Giants' first four possessions of the second half. They had a 27-13 lead with just over 11 minutes left and couldn't win. The Commanders couldn't make a play against Jameis Winston to clinch a victory. And with a chance to ice the game with a 27-20 lead or win the game in the final 1:43 of regulation or after a missed Giants field goal in overtime, the Commanders punted three times. Those were failures too and can't be forgotten.

And obviously the end of the game was inexcusable. The Commanders were rudderless as the clock ran out, and that's alarming. Quinn doesn't call offensive or defensive plays so a stupefying failure in clock management at the end is a really bad look for him. Daniels has to be more aware as well. It's not impossible for the Commanders to rebound from blowing a shot at a win Sunday, but it was embarrassing and will affect them all season in the NFC East race, if they ever get back in it.

Beating the Titans this season doesn't mean a whole lot. But at least the Texans looked good doing it. Their defense gave up a 58-yard drive and a field goal on Tennessee's first possession of the game. The rest of the day, the Texans allowed no points, 129 yards and no drive longer than 27 yards. C.J. Stroud played well, and while the running game still lagged at 2.9 yards per carry, it was good enough on offense.

The next question is whether Marvin Harrison Jr. can help the offense. The Texans must think so considering they sent a second- and seventh-round pick to Arizona for Harrison and a sixth-round pick. They need some punch in the offense. It's questionable if Harrison can come in and be an impact player in the middle of the season after having just five catches for 85 yards and a touchdown for Arizona in 2026. It's tough for any receiver to learn an offense and establish chemistry with a quarterback during a season. However, if it works it could transform Houston's offense. That's the Texans' gamble.

Playing right after an international game is not easy. The Colts took a step back in Sunday's loss at Pittsburgh and it's fair to blame playing in London in Week 4. They missed tackles, especially on two long touchdowns by Jaylen Warren that turned the game around, and they repeatedly settled for field goals in the red zone. Indianapolis had improved in some areas over Weeks 3 and 4, but nothing looked good in a 34-22 loss to the Steelers .

"Go back to the fundamentals of technique," Colts head coach Shane Steichen said via the team's site, regarding tackling . "It was good last week, and then this week it wasn't as good as it needs to be, and so we got to keep working hard on that."

Next up for the Colts is a home game against the Titans, and that needs to be a win because after that they face road games against the 5-0 Vikings and 4-1 Jaguars.

The Browns were close to a much better day. Receiver Isaiah Bond was pressed into action after KC Concepcion's concussion and he had a big drop in a big moments and once ran out of bounds when it seemed he could have pushed upfield for more yardage. One drop came in the end zone and another was on a second-and-19 that could have given the Browns a first down just ahead of the two-minute warning. Those plays were huge in a five-point loss.

Still, the Browns failed to top 200 yards against a Jets defense that had just given up 492 yards to a Tyson Bagent-led Bears offense. Cleveland's 3-1 start came with some close wins and the Browns were due some regression. Week 6's game against the Ravens, who may be without Lamar Jackson, will be telling.

With a minute to go in regulation, the Falcons led by eight points at home against a backup quarterback. The Ravens came back to win in overtime and the Falcons will look at that as a game that they should have won.

Now the Falcons have to worry about Michael Penix Jr. It was disheartening for the team and Penix that the quarterback was unavailable for overtime because of a rib injury suffered on a hard hit late in regulation. Penix has a long injury history dating back to college. He missed the first two games of this season while recovering from his third torn ACL. Even if Penix is available for the Falcons' next game, the injury issue isn't going away, and the Falcons have already shown they're one of the NFL's worst teams without him.

The Cowboys are blowing a good opportunity in a bad NFC East. They gave away a game against the Ravens by mismanaging the final seconds of regulation. They lost at home last week as a big favorite to a Buccaneers team with an undrafted rookie quarterback.

The problem isn't hard to diagnose, and it's the defense. The Cowboys are 32nd in defensive DVOA, the exact spot they held last season. New coordinator Christian Parker hasn't been any better than old coordinator Matt Eberflus and the personnel additions haven't changed anything either. Team owner Jerry Jones gave the odd reason when he traded Micah Parsons that improving the run defense was a major part of the decision; the Cowboys have allowed an NFL-worst 842 rushing yards. Jones is already being asked if he'll remove Parker, and while the answer has been no, the Cowboys did add longtime defensive coach Mike Pettine to the staff this week .

Give the Eagles this: They battled hard in London and after 59:52 it looked like they would beat the Jaguars, who are one of the best teams in football this season. It was easily the Eagles' best performance this season. Absolutely nobody in Philadelphia wants to hear that after the last eight seconds , in which the Eagles kicked off, allowed a 53-yard return and a 57-yard field goal to inexplicably lose. The decision to let the Jaguars have a shot at a return was a clear mistake.

"I didn't make the right decision and I lost us that game," Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said, via the team's site . "And that's what I said to our guys. And what hurts there is that the guys fought so hard and then I don't make the decision that I should make at the end of the game and I cost us that game and I put that fully on me."

Sirianni won a Super Bowl two seasons ago. Since then, the Eagles had a disappointing and drama-filled 2025 season and this season they're 2-3, with the two wins coming late against teams who are a combined 1-8-1. Add in the end of Sunday's game and Sirianni might be in trouble soon. Doug Pederson was fired three seasons after his Super Bowl win, for reference.

Through all the (justifiable) angst over the Packers' start, they're 3-2 coming off a blowout win over the Bears, who were the favorite to win the division. The Packers looked mostly poor during the first four weeks but they find themselves in a good place now.

There are things to clean up, but the trio of Jordan Love, Matthew Golden and Christian Watson might keep Green Bay in the playoff race. Love has played well despite little help from his offensive line, and on Sunday he had a great game with 367 yards. He completed five passes of 30 or more air yards, only the second time that has happened since ESPN Insights began tracking the stat. Golden has 397 yards and two touchdowns and Watson has been even better, with 474 yards and six touchdowns in five games.

"We kept our foot on the gas," Love said after the eye-opening 31-7 win over Chicago, according to AP . "Matt [LaFleur] was dialing it up. That's what it needs to look like, right there."

Aaron Rodgers' stat line isn't perfect. His 59.8 completion percentage is the worst of his career as a starter. So is his 88.9 passer rating. But what he's doing at his age has been approached only by Tom Brady.

Not counting Brady, whose production in his 40s is an extreme outlier, no quarterback in his age-43 season (Rodgers turns 43 in December) has ever had more than 952 passing yards or six touchdowns in a season. Their teams combined for two wins in their starts, and both were from Vinny Testaverde in 2007. Testaverde had a bad 65.8 passer rating that season. Rodgers already has 1,234 yards, 10 touchdowns and the Steelers have won three of his starts, more than every other quarterback at his age combined, other than Brady.

Whatever happens the rest of this season, Rodgers' season is already historic for his age.

The Giants should feel good to get a half of a win after Washington completely blew the end of the game, but New York blew a chance to win itself. In overtime they missed a 46-yard field goal and Cam Skattebo fumbled at Washington's 24-yard line. A tie felt like a win at the end, but that got the Giants off the hook for their own mistakes.

One absolute positive from the game was Malik Nabers. He followed up a 112-yard game by getting season highs with 11 catches and 121 yards. He scored the game-tying touchdown in the final two minutes of regulation. Even more encouraging, he played a season-best 89.9% of New York's snaps. He had not surpassed 80% in the first four games. It's safe to say Nabers is back to normal after last season's ACL tear.

David Tepper shouldn't get too many flowers for becoming a somewhat rational team owner, but he could have considered a coaching change after Dave Canales was 6-15 to start his time with the Panthers. Tepper had been going through coaches like paper plates before then. But ownership stayed the course and Canales has turned it around. He gave up play-calling duties to offensive coordinator Brad Idzik, and that setup has been a success. Bryce Young is having a career year, and even getting mentioned in early MVP conversations. Carolina's offense entered Week 5 ranking fourth in the NFL in both points and yards despite major offensive line injuries.

That looks great on Idzik, who could be a hot name in the head-coaching carousel next offseason if this continues. It also reflects well on Canales for recognizing what needed to change for the Panthers to improve after backing into an NFC South championship last season.

For a 3-2 team, the Broncos should probably be lower in the rankings. The winless Chargers had numerous injury issues Sunday and yet the Broncos still trailed 17-10 with less than 10 minutes left. The Chargers' decision to go for it on fourth-and-1 at their own 41, and then not converting a quarterback sneak, turned around the game. The Broncos deserve credit for stopping that streak and rallying to win, but anyone thrilled with where the Broncos are after five games is ignoring the problem signs.

One of those problems could be Bo Nix. The Broncos are considered to have one of the NFL's best offensive lines. They have enough at receiver including Jaylen Waddle, whom Denver traded a first-round draft pick to acquire. Head coach Sean Payton took over play-calling duties, and that didn't immediately change the offense. When is Nix's role in the woes going to be examined? His passer rating has gone from 93.3 to 87.8 to 80.8 in his first three seasons. On Sunday, with Payton back calling plays, Nix had 123 yards passing against a decent Chargers defense that was without star safety Derwin James Jr. The Broncos can't change play-callers again. Nix needs to perform better. It doesn't get easier with a matchup against the Seahawks on Thursday night.

The Lions' defense is likely to still be a problem, even though it played well against the Cardinals. Detroit's offense is just fine. Jared Goff has 12 touchdowns and no interceptions through five games, which puts him in rare company.

But the engine of the offense is Jahmyr Gibbs. He leads the NFL with 747 yards from scrimmage and nine total touchdowns. That's a pace of 30.6 touchdowns, in range to challenge LaDainian Tomlinson's single-season record of 31. Gibbs didn't deny he has eyes on that record.

"Oh, yeah, for sure. Yeah, I'm trying," Gibbs said, via MLive .

An early East Coast start against a Patriots team that felt energized after a win over the Bills was a tough spot for the Raiders. Still, it was a troubling performance on both sides of the ball. The Raiders' offense didn't get much going, and averaging 2.1 yards per carry was a big reason. Perhaps Ashton Jeanty, who was a game-time decision with foot and ankle injuries, should have sat for a week. He had 27 yards on 10 carries. Vegas' defense was shredded by Drake Maye, who had 374 yards and four touchdowns passing and another one rushing. The Raiders' defense hadn't been bad through four weeks, so it can be excused to a tough day against a good quarterback who is starting to heat up.

It's one bad game after four promising ones, so it's not time to panic. But the next two games will tell the story: The Raiders host the Bills and Rams the next two weeks.

Drake Maye isn't a bad quarterback. Go figure. After naysayers got their licks in during Maye's three-game slump to start the season, which was an extension of his postseason issues, Maye has 643 passing yards, seven passing touchdowns, 79 rushing yards and a rushing score in his last two games. Those games came against the Bills and Raiders, who had one combined loss before facing New England. Stunning, but a 24-year-old quarterback who was one vote from winning MVP last season might still be good .

"It's just fun to see Drake smiling big on the sidelines," Patriots linebacker Robert Spillane said, via SB Nation . "That confidence is obviously back, and just watching him lead and push the ball down the field was fun."

The Rams can play the what-if game. What if Week 1 hadn't been in Australia? What if the officials had gotten a flubbed defensive pass interference call right at Denver in Week 3? And what if Harrison Mevis' field goal hadn't gotten blocked in overtime on Monday against the Bills ? But they are also a veteran team and know the NFL is a results business. A team that got heaps of Super Bowl hype all offseason is 2-3.

The special teams is a recurring problem. The blocked field goal Monday night could be looked at as a bad break for many teams, but the Rams' special teams have been a problem for a while. Huge special teams mistakes led to losses in their final two games against the Seahawks last season, including in the NFC championship game. It shouldn't be a surprise that the special teams let them down with the game on the line Monday.

Joe Burrow wasn't too thrilled after Sunday's win over the Dolphins. His assessment of the team after five games? "Gotta be better. Gotta be better," Burrow said, according to transcripts . When asked in what ways the Bengals need to be better, he said, "Everywhere."

"I think just not good enough all around, team-wide," Burrow said. "I think if we want to be the team that we think we're going to be, you got to be better than that."

The Bengals didn't play that bad. It speaks to how poor the Dolphins are that leading 28-10 into the fourth quarter isn't good enough. But Burrow is trying to get his team to a higher level, which is reasonable going into their bye. The first game back from the bye is huge. The Bengals go to Baltimore to face the Ravens.

It's hard to rank the Bears. On one hand, they were horrendous in a 31-7 loss to the Packers. Also, they have scored 60 points in four games since scoring 59 in the opener. They've had two games scoring seven or fewer points. A defense that had been playing well gave up too many big plays against the Packers, who had 358 yards passing.

Of course, everything will change soon when Caleb Williams comes back. It's unfair to judge a team too harshly when it went 2-1 with two different backup quarterbacks. And Williams is close to returning from a hamstring injury.

"He's on track," Bears head coach Ben Johnson said, via Bears Wire . "We'll see if that's Atlanta [for Week 6] or after. I think it's going to be close."

Once Williams returns, it'll be easier to get a clear read on the Bears.

Justin Jefferson's return changed the Vikings' offense. Not many receivers are capable of making the circus catch he did for a touchdown with three Saints defenders in his vicinity.

The offense playing its best game, in the first game this season that Kyler Murray and Jefferson were healthy throughout, was a big story. The other one is the Vikings' unrelenting blitz strategy. Coordinator Brian Flores sent a blitz on 23 of 27 Saints dropbacks (85.2%), according to Pro Football Focus . New Orleans had 87 net passing yards and 142 total yards. Blitzing as much as this season's Vikings have is a fascinating experiment, and there's no sign the Vikings are going to ease off it.

Moving the Seahawks down this far after a home loss to our No. 1 team is probably too punitive. The Seahawks will likely move up soon. But they are just 3-2.

One move that hasn't gotten enough criticism is letting Kenneth Walker III leave in free agency. Walker is an NFL MVP candidate for the Chiefs. He has transformed their offense and been one of the best players in the league. Meanwhile the Seahawks' running game is floundering. A fumble by George Holani deep in Seahawks territory that was recovered for a 49ers touchdown epitomized a running game going nowhere. Seattle is 30th in EPA per rush play. First-round draft pick Jadarian Price going on IR hasn't helped but he was struggling before his injury.

"That's a position where you can find guys," Seahawks general manager John Schneider said in March to 710 Seattle Sports , regarding Walker's departure.

It's hard to criticize the Seahawks, who were a tremendous champion last season and will be good again. But letting Walker go looks like a big mistake.

The Jaguars did not play well in London. Head coach Liam Coen's passing on short field goals twice, and the Jaguars' failure to convert on fourth down either time looked like it was going to be the story coming out of a 17-16 loss. Then in the final eight seconds the Jaguars got a long kickoff return and kicked a field goal for a 19-17 win over the Eagles.

"Guys stayed the course and we ended up squeaking away with a win," Coen said, according to the team's site . "It ain't pretty, but it's gritty. That's what it comes down to. It's what this team has been. It's what the team is. I love that group."

That's life in the NFL. Questionable decisions fade away when a team wins, even when it's a miracle. The Jaguars stay in London and face the 1-4 Texans next Sunday in a game that could give Jacksonville a massive lead in the division just six weeks into the season.

Sunday night's Ravens win can carry them for a long time . The Ravens won on the road without Lamar Jackson, despite trailing by eight points with a minute to go in regulation. Tyler Huntley came through when it was needed but the Ravens needed a lot more than just Huntley. They rushed for 208 yards. The defense wasn't perfect but did a fair job holding down a hot Falcons offense — seven of Atlanta's 23 points came off a defensive touchdown.

Sunday night's comeback win felt like it made up for the one loss when they let down in the fourth quarter against the Saints, and Jackson's ankle injury isn't considered a long-term issue. A win like Sunday could be a turning point in Baltimore's season.

"That's a big step for our team," Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said, according to the team's transcripts . "And if we let it be, it can be a launch point for us to really, really get this thing rolling."

Josh Allen is one of the few players for which it doesn't really matter what's going on around him. He's always going to give the Bills a chance to win. Allen did need one assist on Monday night at the Rams and got it when linebacker Greg Rousseau blocked a field goal in overtime. That, and Allen's dramatic play that included several key runs (he had 121 yards rushing), was enough to overcome a defense that couldn't get a key stop, another quiet night from Dalton Kincaid and an injury that kept DJ Moore out, two fumbles by James Cook, including a big one in overtime, and everything else. Allen has one MVP and Monday night should position himself as the favorite to win another. The Bills are a flawed team, particularly on defense, but Allen is playing at such a high level they're still 4-1 and clearly a Super Bowl contender.

Jets pass rusher David Bailey is the leading early contender to win NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year after his three sacks on Sunday, bringing him to five on the season. But Chiefs cornerback Mansoor Delane has a case too.

Delane is off to a great start to his pro career. Entering Monday, he ranked fourth among all cornerbacks in Pro Football Focus' grades. According to PFF he has allowed just nine catches for 80 yards in three games (he missed one because of injury). Quarterbacks have a 46.5 passer rating when throwing his way. Delane was a polarizing pick after the Chiefs traded a third- and fifth-round pick to move up three spots and take Delane sixth overall. It seemed like an overpay. But the Chiefs have to be thrilled with what they've seen so far.

A win at Seattle leaves no doubt who is the No. 1 team after five weeks. The 49ers have played very well. Their offense being hyper efficient should have been expected. Their defense, even with Nick Bosa playing just two games and having no sacks, has been the big surprise.

The 49ers are fourth in defensive DVOA, fourth in EPA allowed per play, ninth in success rate allowed, third in points allowed and sixth in yardage allowed. The key has been the linebacker play of Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw, though Greenlaw was ejected and suspended one game for head-butting helmet-less Seahawks linebacker Ernest Jones IV on Sunday. The 49ers lost defensive coordinator Robert Saleh in the offseason and that could have been a big blow after Saleh did a tremendous job last season. But new coordinator Raheem Morris is also doing an excellent job.

articles.title: NFL Trade Pitch Sees Steelers Acquire $8 Million Playmaker to Replace Michael Pittman Jr.
articles.summary: Could the Pittsburgh Steelers acquire veteran wideout Jauan Jennings from the Minnesota Vikings to replace injured Michael Pittman Jr.? The post NFL Trade Pi...
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers will turn to rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard with three other wideouts set to miss Sunday's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The first-year wideout appears ready for a bigger role. But it wouldn't be a bad idea for the Steelers to also acquire a receiver before the NFL trade deadline.

An intriguing trade option for the Steelers has emerged from the Minnesota Vikings — Jauan Jennings.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport said on The Pat McAfee Show on Tuesday that Jennings is a player to keep an eye on in the trade market. Rapoport proposed the San Francisco 49ers as a landing spot for the veteran receiver.

But with Michael Pittman Jr., Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek all injured, the Steelers should consider a Jennings trade.

Why the Steelers Should Inquire About Vikings WR Jauan Jennings

Pittman, who was supposed to start for the Steelers this season, is currently on injured reserve with a foot injury. He will miss at least three more games.

If Pittman returns in three contests, he will be back in the lineup just after the NFL trade deadline. Should the Steelers not see the veteran ready to be back around then, though, it would make a lot of sense for Pittsburgh to target Jennings.

The 29-year-old is not working out in Minnesota. Jennings has fallen behind young wideouts Tai Felton and Myles Price on the team's depth chart. In four games this season, Jennings has just two catches for nine yards.

The Vikings are contending in the NFC North. But they could move forward with Felton and Price as their depth receiving options behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison . The Vikings have also added to their receiver depth recently with Odell Beckham Jr. and took a look at JuJu Smith-Schuster in a tryout this week .

Jennings could be expendable with the Vikings soon. Heavy Sports proposes the Steelers offer a conditional fifth-round pick for the 29-year-old. Such a deal would allow the Vikings to recoup something for the $8 million they invested into the receiver. The Steelers could get a veteran receiver while protecting themselves from disaster with a conditional offer.

The conditions could include a minimum offensive snaps or games played.

Two years ago, Jennings was a 900-yard receiver with the 49ers. He registered 55 catches, 643 receiving yards and nine touchdowns in San Francisco last year.

Jennings could provide the Steelers receiver room the veteran presence Pittman can't at the moment.

Pittsburgh's WR Injuries Entering Week 6

Pittman landed on IR on Saturday , but a lower-body injury has plagued the wideout since August. It's not clear the receiver has dealt with the same foot injury that entire time. If the Steelers have concerns about Pittman getting back on the field this season, though, a trade for someone like Jennings would make a lot of sense.

On a 1-year, $8 million deal, he would be a rental player. That's all the Steelers might need, as Pittman is signed next season, and Bernard could be a capable starter by 2027.

This week, the Steelers will also be missing Wilson and Skowronek. Head coach Mike McCarthy ruled out both for Week 6 while speaking to reporters Monday.

Neither receiver might be out long term. But as long as they're sidelined, the Steelers won't have another experienced receiver besides D.K. Metcalf.

The team will likely elevate Brandon Smith from the practice squad for Sunday's matchup. Smith has played four NFL games in his career.

Jennings would obviously bring a lot more experience. He would do that for Pittsburgh at an affordable price. Acquiring him also wouldn't change any long-term plans the Steelers have at wideout.

articles.title: 3-round Titans mock draft
articles.summary: Conducting a 3-round Tennessee Titans mock draft in 2027 because they are currently slated to own the No. 1 pick.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans are currently slated to possess the No. 1 overall selection in the 2027 NFL Draft. After Week 5, they are winning the SOS tiebreaker versus the other 0-5 teams (Chargers, Dolphins). The Titans do look like legitimate contenders to earn the top pick, unfortunately.

That has prompted this 3-round Titans mock draft. Titans GM Mike Borgonzi (or someone else?) will have difficult decisions to make if they actually end up owning the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft.

Round 1 (No. 1): Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State

Would the Titans draft a quarterback No. 1 overall to replace Cam Ward? Personally, we're currently unimpressed by this upcoming QB class. Arch Manning and Dante Moore haven't been good enough. The Titans may have to decide between choosing a QB to replace the current No. 1 overall quarterback, or a wide receiver who makes the rookie fourth overall pick a WR2.

Jeremiah Smith is a generational prospect and the Titans shouldn't overthink it, if given the opportunity. He looks like a legitimate Hall of Fame talent. Adding Smith to this offense would give Ward even fewer excuses in 2027. If the Titans have to draft a QB in 2028, inheriting Smith is a good problem for that rookie passer to have.

Round 2 (No. 35): Clev Lubin, EDGE, Louisville

Jeffery Simmons is the only Titans pass rusher currently capable of getting after the quarterback. The edge-rushing group is particularly bad. Jermaine Johnson II is on an expiring contract. Femi Oladejo doesn't look like he'll ever be more than a rotational player. Keldric Faulk is still growing and developing, but he's more of a "BIG END" ala Arik Armstead in Robert Saleh's system as opposed to a game-wrecking pass rusher.

Louisville's Clev Lubin is an exciting pass rusher. He proved capable of handling better competition by registering 8.5 sacks in 2025 after having 9.5 sacks at Coastal Carolina in 2024. Lubin already has another four sacks in 2026.

Both Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears are on expiring contracts. The Titans shouldn't bring either player back in 2027. The offense's inability to consistently run the football is hurting Cam Ward.

If the Titans decide to give Ward one final opportunity in 2027, they'll need a significant investment at running back. BYU's LJ Martin is a good-sized back (6-2, 225) with a three-year period of excellent production. Martin is currently my fifth-ranked RB in this class.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson Injury Update, Latest Rumors on Ravens QB's Status for NFL Week 6 vs. Browns
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson could be back on the field in time for a Week 6 matchup against the Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson could be back on the field in time for a Week 6 matchup against the Cleveland Browns.

Jackson has a "realistic chance to return for Sunday's game at Cleveland," ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Wednesday.

Jackson was out for Week 5 as Tyler Huntley led the Ravens to an overtime win at the Atlanta Falcons.

He initially left Week 4's 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans with an ankle injury and didn't play in the second half, a concerning development for a Ravens' offense very much reliant on the dynamic quarterback's unique skill set.

While the Ravens didn't believe at the time it was going to be a long-term issue, there was uncertainty over his short-term availability.

"I really don't think it's going to be crazy long term, but we'll see what happens," head coach Jesse Minter told reporters at the time.

There's no replacing a two-time MVP and three-time first-team All-Pro like Jackson, though the Ravens do have an experienced backup in Huntley.

"There's one Lamar Jackson, the guy's a two-time MVP," Minter said after Week 4. "And so I think for anybody to have to say we're being compared to Lamar is unfair and not realistic. I think [Huntley] as a backup quarterback in this league and even as a starter at times has shown the ability to come in and really kind of run the offense, make plays with his legs, be able to make plays on third down."

Injuries were also a concern for Jackson last season, as he missed four games due to a hamstring injury and a back contusion. Huntley started two of those games, leading the team to a 2-0 record. But the Ravens are obviously a much more dangerous team with a healthy Jackson.
